title: Mapping the Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Sustainable Finance: A TCCM-Driven Bibliometric Analysis and Conceptual Framework
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) and sustainable finance are increasingly intersecting, yet research at their intersection remains fragmented and theoretically underdeveloped. This study combines bibliometric analysis with the Theory–Context–Characteristics–Methodology (TCCM) framework to examine 61 PRISMA-screened articles retrieved from Web of Science. No publication-year restriction was applied; the included corpus spans 2021 to July 2025. Publication output within the corpus increased from seven articles in 2023 to fifteen in 2024, while the 2025 count covers only the period up to the July search date. China accounts for the largest share based on the corresponding author’s country. Stakeholder Theory is the most frequently applied theoretical lens (10 studies), followed by the Resource-Based View (7 studies) and Institutional Theory (5 studies). Within the thematic map, ESG and artificial intelligence occupy the motor-theme quadrant, whereas green finance lies in the emerging-or-declining quadrant. Building on the TCCM synthesis, the study develops a dual-level conceptual framework grounded in the Resource-Based View and Institutional Theory. The framework proposes that AI-related capabilities may contribute to sustainability outcomes through absorptive capacity, green-innovation processes, and supply-chain efficiency, and positions institutional quality, environmental uncertainty, ownership type, and industry competitiveness as boundary conditions. Overall, the study provides a structured theoretical synthesis and a theory-informed agenda for future research at the AI-sustainable finance nexus.

title: Research on the impact of resource dependence and green finance on the efficiency of green development
summary: Abstract Resource dependence entrenches environmental inefficiency in resource-based cities, yet whether green finance can mitigate this structural lock-in remains unclear. Using a balanced panel of 113 prefecture-level cities in China from 2007 to 2022, we measure green development efficiency via a super-SBM model. We find that resource dependence significantly undermines green development efficiency, but this adverse effect is attenuated by green finance and becomes statistically insignificant at high levels of green-finance penetration. Further analysis highlights industrial-structure adjustment and green technological innovation as two important transmission channels. Heterogeneity analysis reveals substantial variation across city development stages and regions, with the moderating effect particularly evident in mature-stage and declining-stage cities and a comparatively larger estimate in northwestern China. Results remain robust under alternative efficiency indicators, lagged-outcome specifications, and instrumental-variable estimations. Moreover, a comparison with non-resource-based cities confirms that this moderating role is contingent on a highly resource-dependent economic structure. Thus, green finance can be viewed as a targeted structural-corrective tool for resource-dependent contexts, rather than merely a one-size-fits-all environmental subsidy. These insights offer important policy implications for differentiated green finance deployment in resource-based regions.

title: Gender Diversity on Corporate Boards: A Corporate Governance and Regulatory Perspective
summary: Over the years, regulatory reforms have increasingly mandated the inclusion of women on corporate boards, resulting in a significant rise in the representation of women directors. This transformation has been driven not only by considerations of social equity and inclusiveness but also by growing recognition of the economic and strategic value of board gender diversity. Existing literature, supported by various social, psychological and organisational theories, consistently highlights board gender diversity as a positive influence on corporate decision-making and governance effectiveness. This study provides a comprehensive review of the evolving research landscape on board gender diversity by examining the available scientific literature from multiple perspectives. It identifies the leading countries, influential authors, seminal publications and prominent academic journals that have shaped this field of research. In addition, the study analyses the relationship between board gender diversity and key corporate outcomes, including financial performance, corporate social responsibility (CSR), environmental performance and sustainability disclosures. A distinctive contribution of this study is its use of the Scopus database for bibliometric mapping, whereas most earlier bibliometric reviews in this domain have predominantly relied on the Web of Science database. By employing Scopus, the study offers a broader and more comprehensive understanding of the intellectual structure, research trends and emerging directions in the literature on board gender diversity, thereby providing valuable insights for future research.

title: STATE POLICY AND INCENTIVE MECHANISMS FOR DEVELOPING THE DIGITAL ECONOMY IN UZBEKISTAN
summary: This article provides a comprehensive analysis of the systemic reforms implemented by the state to develop the digital economy in the Republic of Uzbekistan, the establishment of the legal and regulatory framework, and the role of these measures in ensuring macroeconomic stability. It examines-from both scientific and practical perspectives - the mechanisms for accelerating digital transformation, the digitalization of state services, and the incentives and preferences created to attract foreign investment to the IT sector. The article concludes with proposals and recommendations for further stimulating the digital sector and developing cybersecurity and regional infrastructure.

title: ESG Performance and Earnings Management: Evidence from Chinese Listed Firms
summary: This study examines whether prior environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance is associated with subsequent accrual-based and real earnings management among Chinese A-share listed non-financial firms over 2015–2024. The temporally ordered design measures ESG performance at t?1, earnings management at t, and background covariates at t?2, yielding earnings-management outcomes from 2017 onward. Accrual-based earnings management (AEM) is measured by the absolute value of Modified Jones discretionary accruals, while real earnings management (REM) is captured by a signed composite of abnormal production costs, operating cash flows, and discretionary expenses. ESG performance is measured using a composite constructed from eight rating providers. Pooled ordinary least squares (OLS) models include Hybrid Industry and Year fixed effects with firm-clustered standard errors. The results show that stronger prior ESG performance is associated with a lower subsequent magnitude of AEM and lower subsequent upward-directed REM. The COVID-19 phase analysis shows that neither the During–Pre nor the Post–Pre contrast is statistically significant for the ESG–AEM association, whereas the negative ESG–REM association is significantly more pronounced in the Post period than in the Pre period. The principal full-sample associations remain consistent across the robustness specifications. All findings are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects.

title: From Green-Bond Valuation and Climate-Risk Integration to Investor Stewardship and ESG Credibility
summary: This paper examines the development of sustainable finance through three interconnected dimensions: green bonds, climate-related financial mechanisms, and responsible investment. The literature shows that green bonds have evolved from a specialised financing instrument into a broader mechanism for mobilising capital, signalling environmental commitments, and supporting corporate and public sustainability strategies. However, their financial characteristics remain conditional on market liquidity, issuer credibility, certification, institutional arrangements, and investor preferences. Sustainable finance also extends beyond labelled securities because climate-related physical and transition risks increasingly affect conventional asset prices, banking systems, financial stability, and corporate financing decisions. At the investor level, environmental, social, and governance considerations influence portfolio construction through screening, ESG integration, engagement, stewardship, and impact objectives. Nevertheless, the effectiveness of these strategies is complicated by substantial disagreement among ESG rating providers and by differences in investor objectives. The literature therefore suggests that sustainable finance cannot be assessed exclusively through issuance volumes, ESG scores, or short-term financial performance. Its development depends on the interaction between credible environmental information, financial institutions, corporate behaviour, investor preferences, and regulatory frameworks capable of improving comparability and limiting greenwashing.

title: Supply chain risk and strategic reconfiguration: evidence from China
summary: While globalization has significantly improved supply chain efficiency, it has also increased the exposure of firms to supply chain risks and vulnerabilities. How firms respond to these risks has therefore become an increasingly important question. Using data on Chinese listed firms from 2009 to 2023, this paper constructs a novel firm-year measure of supply chain risk perception based on textual analysis and examines how firms adjust their supplier networks in response to rising uncertainty. This expansion occurs along both domestic and international dimensions, with firms sourcing from a broader set of countries, consistent with a risk diversification strategy. Moreover, firms shift sourcing towards countries with higher government efficiency, suggesting an institutional channel through which firms enhance supply stability. Importantly, our additional evidence provides limited support for the view that the increase in supplier numbers is primarily driven by firms’ business expansion. These findings provide important implications for both firms and policymakers seeking to enhance supply chain resilience in an increasingly uncertain global environment.

title: TRANSPARENCY AND ACCOUNTABILITY IN FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT OF SECONDARY SCHOOLS IN NIGER STATE, NIGERIA
summary: This study examined transparency and accountability in the financial management of secondary schools in Niger State, Nigeria. The study investigated how transparency and accountability influence effective utilization of financial resources in secondary school administration. The research adopted a descriptive survey design involving principals, vice-principals, bursars, and teachers from selected secondary schools in Niger State. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using descriptive and inferential statistics. Findings revealed that transparency in financial reporting, regular auditing, stakeholder participation, and accountability mechanisms significantly improve financial management practices in schools. The study further established that inadequate monitoring, poor record keeping, political interference, and insufficient financial training remain major challenges affecting accountability in school finance management. The study concluded that effective financial management in secondary schools depends largely on transparent procedures and accountability systems. Recommendations include regular auditing, capacity building for school administrators, and stronger government oversight of school finances.

title: Does digital transformation substitute for ESG disclosure? Evidence from Indonesian banking
summary: Sustainability disclosure is widely assumed to raise firm value, and digital transformation to strengthen that relationship. This study questions the second assumption. Drawing on legitimacy theory, we argue that sustainability and digital disclosure are competing rather than complementary legitimation channels: where a bank already signals transparency through extensive digital disclosure, incremental sustainability reporting carries less marginal legitimacy. We test this on a panel of commercial banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during a period of accelerated post-pandemic digitalisation and mandatory sustainability reporting. Fixed-effects estimation, reported alongside pooled and random-effects specifications, indicates that the ESG valuation premium is positive but conditional, declining as digital disclosure intensity rises. It is evident among banks with limited digital disclosure and indistinguishable from zero among the most digitally advanced. Technological disruption shows no detectable association with firm value. Dynamic panel estimation returns no significant evidence on the moderation and is reported as an endogeneity probe rather than confirmation, since the observation window is too short to identify dynamic effects reliably. Because both constructs are measured through disclosure, the substitution documented here may operate between reporting channels rather than underlying capabilities, a boundary we state rather than resolve.

title: Corporate social responsibility and bank risk: theory and empirical evidence
summary: Social responsibility is an important matter that business owners should prioritize. This study analyses data from commercial banks in Vietnam between 2015 and 2024 to examine the impact of corporate social responsibility (CSR) on bank risk. The analysis employs models: The analysis employs Generalized Model of Moment (GMM) and Feasible Generalized GLeast Squares (FGLS) with an unbalanced panel dataset comprising 19 commercial banks. The findings show that CSR contributes to reducing bank risk. The study also provides the theoretical basis for CSR by identifying the influence of each CSR factor on different business risks. Furthermore, it also strengthens the relationship between risk and safe banking practices. The foundation for suggesting practical management implications for risk management in the context of sustainable development.

title: A fair profit distribution as a resilient strategy in supply chains under ripple effect
summary: A fair distribution of profits among primary partners is crucial to promote long-term relationships in global supply chains. In this paper, a fair decision-making is studied in a multi-tier supply chain under propagated disruptions. Instead of a common game-theoretic framework, the fair optimization theory approach is applied to determine an equitably efficient distribution of expected profits among primary partners of a supply chain. A novel stochastic mixed integer program is developed. The fair profit distribution is optimized along with optimal selection of recovery supply portfolios and coordination of production across the supply chain for each disruption scenario to mitigate the impact of the ripple effect. In the supply chain a collaborative partnership is applied to ensure that the expected service level of manufacturer is not less than the service level of each supplier. This study’s contribution and novelty lie in the development of a computationally efficient optimization model for a fair allocation of expected profits in multi-tier supply chains under the ripple effect. The proposed fair optimization approach integrates a multi-tier structure of supply chain, propagated disruptions across the supply chain, recovery portfolio decisions, and the collaborative service requirements. The computational findings indicate that if manufacturer’s objective is to maximize its individual profit, then the associated profits of all primary suppliers may converge to their respective maxima as well as to the fair profit distribution. Moreover, the fair profit distribution under collaborative partnership may ensure coordinated production across the supply chain. Overall, this study demonstrates that supply chain fairness can be a driver of supply chain resiliency. Both, a better coordination of the manufacturer and primary suppliers production, and an efficient collaboration with backup suppliers may improve the supply chain resilience.

title: Confucian Cultural Exposure and Earnings Management in China: Evidence from Accrual-Based and Real Earnings Management
summary: This study examines the association between Confucian cultural exposure and earnings management among Chinese A-share listed non-financial firms over 2015–2024. Drawing on Social Norm Theory, it distinguishes between accrual-based earnings-management magnitude and upward-directed real earnings management. Confucian cultural exposure is measured as the natural logarithm of one plus the number of Confucius temples within 100 kilometres of each firm’s registered location. The principal models employ pooled ordinary least squares with Hybrid Industry and Year fixed effects and firm-clustered standard errors, supplemented by pooled interaction analyses. Confucian cultural exposure is negatively associated with accrual-based earnings-management magnitude, but the association is not statistically significant, providing no support for H1. Its association with upward-directed real earnings management is also negative and provides limited support for H2 at the 10% level. The temporal analysis identifies no statistically significant variation in the accrual-based association. For real earnings management, the association is significantly more negative in 2020–2022 than in 2015–2019, while the 2023–2024 versus 2015–2019 contrast provides weaker evidence at the 10% level. The study extends recent evidence on Confucian cultural exposure and earnings management while highlighting the importance of distinguishing between alternative forms of managerial discretion and formally examining temporal heterogeneity. The results are interpreted as conditional associations rather than causal effects.

title: Family firm heterogeneity and corporate social responsibility: a literature review on internal family governance
summary: Purpose This study summarizes earlier research on the impact of internal family governance on corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance and CSR reporting as a major element of family firm heterogeneity. Design/methodology/approach Relying on a literature review, internal family governance is separated into group-related characteristics (e.g. board level, (top) management level) and individual internal governance attributes (e.g. chief executive officer (CEO) board chair). Fifty-five studies published between 2004 and the present were examined. Potential country effects were analyzed by grouping country-specific studies according to the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD) membership and board structure. Findings Most studies examined the influence of family CEOs on CSR performance, while other aspects of internal family governance – such as family board chair or a family (top) management member – and CSR reporting received less attention. Overall, the relationship between internal family governance and CSR was inconclusive, which is consistent with the two distinct perspectives of socioemotional wealth (SEW) (SEW-as-inspiration and SEW-as-restriction). However, in line with the SEW-as-restriction view, we stress some tendencies toward a negative relationship between group-related family governance and CSR outcomes in non-OECD countries and countries with mandatory one-tier systems. Research limitations/implications Future research on internal family governance and CSR outcomes should recognize the demographic factors, social capital, and human capital of family board and (top) management team members. Among others, the impact of family board members' sustainability skills and networks on CSR should be analyzed in detail. Practical implications Family board and management members should increase their environmental and social expertise to increase the probability of substantive CSR strategies, management systems, and reporting. These efforts should strengthen stakeholder trust and overall family firm reputation. Social implications Stakeholders should carefully examine the quality of internal family governance considering the heterogeneity of family firms and management discretion related to CSR. Originality/value To the best of the author's knowledge, this is the first literature review on internal family governance as a major element of corporate governance and CSR. Moreover, the separation of internal family governance into individual and group-related attributes, CSR performance, and CSR reporting increases the transparency for researchers.

title: Analysis of Strategic Marketing on Sustainable Business in the Finance Industry Performance
summary: The financial services sector is undergoing a significant metamorphosis propelled by the emergence of sustainability concerns, shifting consumer demands, and regulatory adjustments. The goal of this research is to present a thorough examination of the strategic marketing campaigns that influence how well sustainable business practices function in the financial sector. This research adds to a better knowledge of how financial institutions can successfully coordinate their marketing initiatives with sustainable business goals by analyzing the interaction between marketing strategies and sustainability in this setting.Key showcasing is re-imagined in the present VUCA world, which is overwhelmed by unpredictability, vulnerability, intricacy, and equivocalness. As a result, it is necessary to develop robust capabilities for business adaptability and resilience while placing a significant emphasis on the implementation of measures to address social challenges and climate change. Small and medium-sized businesses (SMEs) are using them, but not all of them are successful. Businesses that incorporate ESG programs into changing business models and strategies are typically the ones that initiate and develop them, resulting in sustainable strategic marketing frameworks. Nonetheless, taking on maintainability in business requires all the while acquiring monetary execution and approaching monetary capital that can be spent. The paper analyzes the association between feasible venture rehearses and the ongoing challenges of manageable key showcasing in lined up with scholastic conversations on the production of investor esteem.The results of this study will provide important new information about how strategic marketing shapes sustainable business practices and impacts the performance of the financial industry to stakeholders, including customers, legislators, executives, and marketers.

title: Sustainability Accounting Disclosure and Financial Performance of Listed Consumer Goods Companies in Nigeria
summary: This study investigated whether sustainability accounting disclosures influence the financial performance of consumer goods companies quoted on the Nigerian Exchange Group (NGX). Particular attention was given to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosures and their respective effects on Return on Assets (ROA). An ex post facto research design was employed, using secondary information extracted from audited annual financial statements and sustainability reports of five purposively selected companies covering the 2020–2024 period. The selected firms were Nestlé Nigeria Plc, Cadbury Nigeria Plc, Coca-Cola HBC Nigeria Plc, Guinness Nigeria Plc, and Dangote Sugar Refinery Plc, resulting in a balanced panel dataset comprising 25 firm-year observations. Disclosure indices for environmental, social, and governance information were constructed in line with the GRI Universal Standards (2021). The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and panel-data regression techniques. Both Fixed Effects and Random Effects estimations were performed, while the Hausman specification test was applied to determine the more appropriate model. Findings from the selected Random Effects model indicated that environmental disclosure was positively associated with ROA, although the relationship was not statistically significant. Social disclosure recorded a negative and statistically insignificant relationship with ROA, whereas governance disclosure demonstrated a statistically significant relationship with financial performance. The study consequently underscores the need for listed consumer goods companies to enhance the quality and scope of sustainability-related reporting, with particular emphasis on governance disclosures as an important factor in strengthening corporate financial performance.

title: Can green innovations enhance competitive advantage?
summary: Abstract Sustainable New Product Introductions (SNPIs) enable firms to meet consumers’ increasing demand for sustainable options while addressing rising expectations for corporate environmental responsibility. This study demonstrates that SNPIs can also strengthen brands by enhancing brand equity. Drawing on signaling theory, we propose that SNPIs serve as product-based sustainability signals that enhance brand equity by generating social goodwill. A staggered event study of the initial launch of a sustainable product line by a major laundry detergent brand shows that SNPIs can increase parent-brand equity. A complementary analysis of subsequent SNPIs across 15 leading brands in 12 retail chains reveals that this effect is moderated by parent firms' ethical reputation and retail chains' sustainable assortment share. These findings advance our understanding of whether and under what conditions sustainable products serve as credible signals of environmental responsibility and enhance brand equity.

title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AND INTELLECTUAL CAPITAL DISCLOSURE OF LISTED NON-FINANCIAL FIRMS IN NIGERIA
summary: Firms are required to adequately disclose their corporate information in order to minimize the problem of information asymmetry between the managers and other corporate stakeholders. Notwithstanding the significance of intellectual capital disclosure in the reduction of information asymmetry among corporate stakeholders, information about firm’s intellectual capital is disclosed in the corporate annual reports voluntarily and corporate governance practice plays significant role in the adequacy of voluntary disclosure. In view of this, this study provides empirical evidence of the impact of corporate governance on intellectual capital disclosure using the listed Nigerian non-financial firms as a case study. Corporate governance is represented with Board Size (BS), Board Independence (BI), Board Financial Expertise (BFE), Audit Committee Size (ACS), Audit Committee Independence (ACI) and Audit Committee Financial Expertise (ACFE) while intellectual capital disclosure is measured by intellectual capital disclosure index. Data are collated through secondary source of annual reports of the sampled firms for the period covering 2014-2024 and the results of the fixed-effects regression analysis reveal that BS insignificantly and negatively impacts intellectual capital disclosure (β1BSit = -.0594239, p = 0.150) while BI, BFE, ACS, ACI and ACFE significantly and positively influence intellectual capital disclosure (β2BIit = .1387609, p = 0. 0.000; β3BFEit = .1569342, p = 0.000; β4ACSit = .1984109, p = 0.000; β5ACIit = .1325203, p = 0.003; β6ACFEit = .1298492, p = 0.010). For this reason, the study concludes that corporate governance meaningfully improves intellectual capital disclosure and therefore recommends that regulatory agencies and corporate entities should strengthen corporate governance practice to encourage adequate disclosure of intellectual capital disclosure so that firm’s performance can be enhanced through improvement of information symmetry among stakeholders.

title: STRENGTHENING DIGITAL CITIZENSHIP COMPETENCIES OF PPKn MASTER STUDENTS AS PROSPECTIVE UMKM ENTREPRENEURS: A LEGAL-NORMATIVE REVIEW AND ACTUALIZATION OF PANCASILA ECONOMICS
summary: Digital transformation has reshaped citizenship, higher education, and MSME entrepreneurship in Indonesia. In this context, Master’s students of Pancasila and Civic Education should no longer be positioned merely as prospective educators or academics, but also as digital citizens with the potential to become actors of people-centered entrepreneurship grounded in Pancasila values. The state has established a regulatory framework for the facilitation, protection, and empowerment of MSMEs, including the strengthening of the digital ecosystem; however, digital literacy, digital ethics, legal awareness, and social justice orientation remain substantive challenges (Government of the Republic of Indonesia, 2021; Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs of the Republic of Indonesia, n.d.; “Transformasi Digital UMKM Indonesia,” n.d.). This study aims to analyze a model for strengthening the digital citizenship competence of Master’s students in Pancasila and Civic Education as prospective MSME entrepreneurs through a juridical-normative approach and the perspective of Pancasila economics. The study employs qualitative library research with juridical-normative, philosophical, and conceptual approaches. Data were collected through document studies of legislation, recent academic publications, institutional reports, and relevant scholarly articles, and were analyzed using content analysis and thematic interactive analysis. The findings show that strengthening digital citizenship competence among Master’s students in Pancasila and Civic Education should be constructed through four integrated dimensions: digital-regulatory literacy, digital ethical-participatory capacity, digital social entrepreneurship capacity, and a Pancasila-based economic justice orientation. From the normative perspective, the national legal framework has opened legal and institutional space for MSME digitalization, yet it has not been fully translated into postgraduate civic education designs that prepare students as sovereign, responsible, and justice-oriented actors in the digital economy. This study offers a novelty by reconstructing digital citizenship competence not merely as the ability to use digital media safely and ethically, but as a form of civic-economic competence that connects digital rights, constitutional responsibilities, business legal compliance, and the praxis of people-centered economy in digital spaces (“Strengthening Citizenship Skills,” n.d.; “Strategi Penerapan Ekonomi Pancasila,” n.d.; “Implementasi Pancasila dalam Kebijakan Ekonomi,” n.d.; Government of the Republic of Indonesia, 2021; Coordinating Ministry for Economic Affairs of the Republic of Indonesia, n.d.). The study concludes that Master’s students in Pancasila and Civic Education occupy a strategic position as agents of civic entrepreneurship reform who can bridge civic education, economic law, and national MSME empowerment. The implications point to the need for curriculum reformulation, stronger campus policies, and the development of a Pancasila-based digital civic entrepreneurship learning ecosystem.

title: IMPACT OF INTERNAL CONTROL SYSTEM AND CORPORATE GOVERNANCE ON THE PERFORMANCE OF SELECTED CUSTOMER GOODS FIRMS IN NIGERIA
summary: This study examined the impact of internal control systems and corporate governance on the performance of selected consumer goods firms in Nigeria. An ex post facto research design was adopted using a quantitative approach. The study focused on Nigeria Breweries Plc and Nestlé Nigeria Plc, with secondary data obtained from their published annual reports and accounts covering the period 2015–2024. Firm performance was measured using Return on Assets, while internal control was assessed using an Internal Control Disclosure Index. Corporate governance was measured using board size, board independence, board meetings, audit committee size, audit committee independence, and board gender diversity. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, and panel regression with Stata 17 at a 5% significance level. The findings revealed that internal control systems were positively and statistically significantly related to firm performance (β = 18.432, p = 0.004). Corporate governance mechanisms, particularly board independence, board size, audit committee independence, board meeting frequency, and female board representation, also demonstrated significant positive associations with firm performance. The combined model showed that internal control systems and corporate governance jointly explained 78.3% of the variation in firm performance. The study concludes that integrating robust internal control systems with effective corporate governance practices enhances organizational performance. It recommends strengthening internal controls, board independence, audit committee effectiveness, diversity, and governance oversight among consumer goods firms in Nigeria.

title: Tax Avoidance and Corporate Governance: Mapping the Intellectual Structure, Emerging Trends, and Future Research Frontiers
summary: In spite of a considerable amount of attention being paid to the interaction between tax avoidance and corporate governance across the globe, this study aims to provide a detailed bibliometric evaluation concerning the productivity, performance, and intellectual structure of scientific production on tax avoidance and corporate governance. All data used in this study were gathered from the Scopus database using documents published from 2006 to 2025, which made the total number of documents reach 295. In this study, both VOSviewer and Biblioshiny were used to conduct a bibliometric analysis of this corpus. The findings of this research revealed a remarkable annual increase in publication rate equal to 25.77%, showing an increasing trend in academic research concerning the role of corporate governance in shaping corporate tax avoidance behavior. The most productive journals that have been identified as the main sources are Accounting and Finance, Journal of Corporate Finance, Journal of risk and financial management and Cogent Business and Management. Moreover, Richardson G. and Taylor G. have been found to be the most productive authors in terms of the number of documents published in this field, whereas China, Indonesia, and the USA are the leading countries in terms of the number of affiliated documents. There are seven major clusters discovered based on co-occurrence analysis, among which corporate governance and tax avoidance emerge as the most powerful driving forces. The trending-topics analysis further highlighted that board-gender diversity, CEO compensation and agency problems are the keywords emerging most recently in the field.

title: Reframing Sustainability Reporting Quality Through Digital Transformation: Insights From a Systematic Literature Review
summary: ABSTRACT Digital transformation is reshaping sustainability governance by redefining how firms ensure the integrity of corporate disclosures. While prior research has primarily emphasized process efficiency, limited attention has been paid to sustainability reporting quality (SRQ) as a strategic driver of corporate social responsibility (CSR) accountability. This study develops the tech‐quality reporting (TQR) framework, conceptualizing digital reporting as a dynamic organizational capability that enables firms to systematically enhance reporting quality. Through a systematic literature review and qualitative content analysis, the framework explains how digital technologies such as blockchain and artificial intelligence strengthen firms' ability to identify environmental, social, and governance (ESG) risks, seize technological opportunities, and transform reporting practices. By aligning technological capabilities with the Global Reporting Initiative reporting quality principles, the study positions SRQ as a strategic lever for credible ESG reporting and long‐term corporate accountability within evolving sustainability ecosystems, thereby contributing to the emerging literature on digital transformation in CSR.

title: ESG SUSTAINABILITY DISCLOSURES AND MARKET-BASED VALUATION IN AN EMERGING ECONOMY: EVIDENCE FROM LISTED NIGERIAN OIL AND GAS FIRMS IN NIGERIA
summary: This study examines the effect of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) sustainability disclosure on share price of listed oil and gas companies in Nigeria over ten-year period covering 2016 to 2025. The research employed three dimensions of sustainability disclosures, Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) while share price form the Proxy of the dependent variable (Market performance Valuation). The research used an ex-post factor research design, with population consisting of all the eleven (11) listed oil and gas companies in Nigeria as of 31st December 2025. Judgmental Sampling technique was used in selecting only (7) seven oil firms whose report are up to the study reporting date. Data was sourced from secondary sources, since this is a quantitative research grounded on the positivist paradigm. The analysis was conducted using the two-step system GMM estimation technique, which addressed the dynamic nature of firm performance and controlled for potential endogeneity. However, the findings of the GMM analysis revealed that only environmental and social sustainability had a statistically significant impact on market-based performance, as measured by share price. While Governance disclosure were not statistically significant on share price of listed oil and gas firms. Although the coefficients for the indicators of the variables (Governance Sustainability) were having positive signed in the baseline model (Model One) however, the p-values of the variable (Governance disclosures) exceeded the 5% threshold for significance. In line with the findings it was concluded that, high or low levels of information asymmetry do always alter how investors interpret sustainability disclosures. Based on the findings and conclusions, the study recommended among other things that, given the broader dimension of direct effects of the study variables, capital market stakeholders should initiate collaborative ESG education and policy reform efforts to help companies improve ESG disclosure practices.

title: ADAPTATION STRATEGIES OF SMEs IN IMPROVING COMPETITIVENESS IN THE DIGITAL ECONOMY ERA IN DENPASAR CITY
summary: This study aims to analyze the adaptation strategies of Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) in improving competitiveness in the digital economy era in Denpasar City. The rapid development of digital technology has changed business competition patterns, consumer behavior, marketing systems, transaction models, and internal business management practices. SMEs are required to adapt not only by using digital platforms, but also by improving managerial capacity, product innovation, service quality, digital marketing, collaboration networks, human resource capability, and employee loyalty. In Denpasar City, SMEs have an important role in supporting the local economy, especially in sectors related to trade, culinary businesses, services, creative products, and tourism-supporting activities. However, many SMEs still face challenges such as limited digital literacy, lack of access to technology, limited capital, weak branding, low ability to utilize data-based marketing, and limited employee readiness in responding to digital transformation. This study uses a qualitative descriptive approach based on secondary data analysis. Data were collected through journal articles, government reports, statistical data, previous research findings, and relevant supporting documents related to SME digital adaptation, competitiveness, and employee loyalty. The research focuses on SMEs in Denpasar City that have implemented digital adaptation strategies in their business activities. The results of this study indicate that SME adaptation strategies include the use of social media for promotion, participation in digital marketplaces, digital payment adoption, product innovation, improvement of customer service, strengthening of business networks, and development of employee capability and loyalty. Employee loyalty becomes an important internal factor because loyal employees can support service consistency, customer relationship management, operational stability, and the implementation of digital business practices. These strategies can help SMEs expand market reach, improve operational efficiency, build stronger customer relationships, strengthen internal resources, and increase competitiveness. This study is expected to provide practical recommendations for SME actors and local government in strengthening SME competitiveness in the digital economy era.

title: Digital Transformation in the Electrical Manufacturing Industry: A Literature Review of Key Considerations and Strategic Priorities
summary: This paper reviews the digital transformation landscape confronting the electrical manufacturing industry, examining the technological, operational, and strategic considerations that determine successful adoption. Drawing on industry reports, case studies, and recent literature, the study synthesizes emerging technology trends, including advanced connectivity, the Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, and big-data analytics, and their implications for electrical businesses transitioning toward Industry 4.0 practices. A risk framework is developed to categorize the principal threats and opportunities facing the sector, addressing challenges such as legacy-system interoperability, networking infrastructure gaps, high capital requirements, supply chain disruptions, and evolving data-governance regulations. Successful transformation practices from established organizations, including P&G, GE Digital, Schneider Electric, and Enel X, are examined to extract lessons applicable to the electrical manufacturing context. The findings indicate that a resilient technology foundation, anchored in enterprise resource planning and a coherent digital ecosystem, underpins sustained transformation, while regulatory, workforce, and infrastructure constraints remain significant barriers. The paper concludes by outlining the digital ambitions and priorities electrical businesses should pursue, including investment in data analytics capabilities, cybersecurity, and low-code/no-code enterprise tools, to remain competitive amid accelerating global sustainability and digitalization targets.

title: AI-Driven Supply Chain Management in Electronics Manufacturing: A Case Study of the BOMate Platform by Foxconn
summary: Artificial intelligence has become an important driver of transformation in supply chain management (SCM). Existing research has focused primarily on consumer-facing contexts and localized applications such as forecasting, inventory, and logistics. Comparatively less attention has been given to how leading manufacturing firms implement AI to support SCM processes in real-world production contexts. To address this gap, this study adopts a case study approach to examine Foxconn’s BOMate platform as an example of AI-enabled supply chain management in advanced electronics manufacturing. The current case in study focuses on the AI-driven platform design principles which integrate experts’ rules, big data and AI modeling to augment procurement decision-making. The findings illustrate that BOMate contributes to SCM in several important ways. First, it augments human decision-making by combining expert rules, accumulated sourcing knowledge, and AI-based processing within a human-AI collaborative framework. Second, it enhances sourcing efficiency by accelerating component retrieval, substitute identification, and decision support. More broadly, the case suggests that AI in Foxconn’s supply chain is not limited to localized automation, but supports system-level coordination across procurement, production, and supply chain operations. This study contributes to the literature by providing empirical insight into AI-enabled SCM in a leading manufacturing firm and highlights the strategic importance of AI in improving supply chain efficiency, resilience, and technological transformation.

title: Understanding the Evolution of Fintech and Sustainable Development: A Comprehensive Review
summary: This article examines the evolution of research at the intersection of financial technology (fintech) and sustainable development through a bibliometric and integrative review of 256 documents indexed in Scopus and Web of Science up to July 2024. The study illustrates the publication trends, influential sources, authors, countries, collaboration patterns, and thematic structures, and sheds light on the evolving knowledge base from a Dynamic Capabilities Theory perspective. The results reveal a significant increase in research starting from 2020, characterised by the emergence of key themes such as financial inclusion, green finance, natural resources, Sustainable Development Goals, and digital financial ecosystems. Thematic and co-occurrence analysis also shows that, across the sample, sustainable finance, Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices, blockchain, big-data analytics and artificial intelligence are increasingly converging with fintech. The review suggests that fintech is not just a financial technology, but a mechanism that enables organisations and financial systems to ‘feel’ opportunities and change regarding sustainability and then capture and digitise them with financial technology, as well as reconfigure financial processes, stakeholder relationships, governance and resources. The study goes beyond the descriptive development of fintech research to highlight implications for firm behaviour, stakeholder relations, governance, innovation, and strategy. It also establishes a research programme on new technologies, climate and green finance, digital inclusion, ESG, governance and organisational transformation towards sustainability.

title: Corporate Sustainability and Firm Value Understanding the Conditions Under Which CSR and ESG Performance Translate into Financial Valuation
summary: This paper examines the relationship between corporate social responsibility (CSR), environmental, social and governance (ESG) performance, and firm value by synthesizing recent theoretical and empirical contributions on corporate sustainability and financial outcomes. The literature indicates that CSR and ESG activities can influence valuation through several interconnected mechanisms, including stakeholder trust, reputational capital, information transparency, operating efficiency, risk reduction, governance quality, access to finance, and resilience during periods of uncertainty. However, the relationship is neither automatic nor uniformly positive. Its magnitude depends on the materiality of sustainability issues, the quality of disclosure, industry exposure, institutional conditions, ownership characteristics, board structures, and the credibility of ESG measurement. Particular attention is given to ESG controversies, carbon risk, sustainability reporting, governance mechanisms, and emerging-market conditions. The evidence also highlights substantial methodological challenges arising from disagreement among ESG rating providers and differences between accounting and market-based performance measures. Overall, the literature suggests that CSR and ESG contribute to firm value when sustainability initiatives are strategically aligned with financially material risks and opportunities, credibly communicated, and supported by effective governance. The paper therefore presents sustainability as a conditional corporate value mechanism rather than a universal source of superior financial performance.

title: Environmental Governance And Oil And Gas Exploration In Nigeria: A Critical Appraisal Of The Legal And Institutional Frameworks
summary: Nigeria's oil and gas industry remains central to national economic development, revenue generation and energy supply, but petroleum exploration and production have also produced persistent environmental challenges, particularly in the Niger Delta.Oil spills, hydrocarbon contamination of soil and water, gas flaring, ecosystem degradation, petroleum waste, biodiversity loss and the National Oil Spill Detection and Response Agency Act, the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency Act and relevant subsidiary regulations.It evaluated the respective meaningful community participation.

title: Beyond awareness: How perceived benefits, risk and trust shape Indian investors' preference and intention toward green investments
summary: Sustainable finance has expanded rapidly in India, yet retail uptake of green investments remains uneven, and little is known about the behavioural factors that shape preference for green over conventional options. This study examines how awareness, perceived benefits, perceived risk and trust influence investment preference, and how that preference translates into behavioural intention to invest in green financial products. Drawing on behavioural finance and ESG literature, a structured questionnaire was administered online to a convenience sample of 250 individual investors, and the proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling in SmartPLS. The measurement model met reliability and validity criteria, and model fit was acceptable (SRMR of 0.062 for the saturated model and 0.074 for the estimated model). Perceived benefits (β = 0.329) and trust (β = 0.269) increased investment preference, while perceived risk reduced it (β = 0.244, negative). Awareness had no significant direct effect (β = 0.107, p = 0.128). Investment preference strongly predicted behavioural intention (β = 0.624), consistent with a mediating role for preference, and the model explained 40.8% of the variance in preference and 38.7% in intention. The findings indicate that knowing about green investments is not enough, and that perceived value, credible ESG disclosure and lower perceived risk matter more. The study adds evidence from an emerging market to behavioural finance and sustainable investing research and offers guidance for policymakers, financial institutions and ESG practitioners.

title: Digital Transformation and the Reconstruction of Social Space in Madagascar
summary: Digital transformation is changing the ways in which information, services, economic transactions, and social relations are organised in Madagascar, but these changes are occurring within pronounced spatial and socioeconomic inequalities. This structured narrative review examines how digital infrastructure and digital practices are associated with the reconstruction of social space in Madagascar, with particular attention to urban-rural differences, device and internet access, mobile-network expansion, education, employment, health, civic participation, and everyday social interaction. Peer-reviewed literature was integrated with primary statistical and policy sources from the Institut National de la Statistique, UNICEF, the Autorité de Régulation des Technologies de Communication, the World Bank, the Ministry of Public Health, and other authoritative institutions. The evidence shows rapid growth in mobile connectivity alongside persistent inequalities in material access and effective use. National survey data indicate marked differences in internet access by residence, while household possession of mobile telephones varies substantially by location, education, and employment characteristics. Telecommunications-regulator reports show a sharp rise in mobile-internet subscriptions and data traffic, but subscription-based indicators cannot be interpreted as counts of unique users. These patterns are consistent with a socio-spatial reading that combines Castells' network perspective, Lefebvre's production of space, and van Dijk's emphasis on unequal material and skills-related access. Digital technologies therefore expand the range of spaces through which social and economic activity can occur without eliminating the importance of place, infrastructure, income, education, and institutional capacity. The review concludes that Madagascar's digital transformation is best understood as an uneven process of spatial extension and reorganisation rather than as a uniform transition to an integrated digital society.

title: From FinTech Intermediation to Blockchain-Based Infrastructures and Institutional Adaptation
summary: This paper examines how FinTech and blockchain technologies are transforming the organization, functioning, and regulation of contemporary financial markets. The literature shows that FinTech modifies financial intermediation through digital platforms, alternative lending, data-driven credit assessment, open banking, digital payments, robo-advisory services, and new forms of competition between banks, FinTech firms, and BigTech companies. Blockchain extends this transformation by introducing distributed recordkeeping, programmable contracts, tokenization, crypto-assets, decentralized finance, and alternative trading and settlement mechanisms. These innovations can reduce information, transaction, reconciliation, and intermediation costs while creating new opportunities for financial inclusion, entrepreneurial financing, and market participation. However, technological transformation also introduces new forms of market fragmentation, volatility, cybersecurity exposure, governance problems, regulatory uncertainty, and environmental externalities. The literature further indicates that cryptocurrencies remain characterized by distinctive pricing dynamics, speculative behavior, changing market efficiency, and conditional diversification properties. Regulatory responses, central bank digital currencies, institutional adaptation, and sustainable technological architectures therefore become central elements of financial-market transformation. Overall, the evidence suggests that digital finance is producing hybrid financial structures in which decentralized technologies increasingly coexist with regulated institutions rather than completely replacing conventional financial intermediaries

title: The spatial effects of digital economy on urban-rural consumption gap: A spatial Durbin model
summary: The high penetration of the digital economy is viewed as a potential for enhancing rural consumption capacity due to its diffusion effect. Related research has limitations such as insufficient theoretical analysis, low data availability, and lack of spatial dimension analysis. Drawing on inclusive growth theory for the local effect and spatial economics for interregional spillovers, this study examines 202 Chinese cities from 2011 to 2019 using a Spatial Durbin Model. The research results indicate that the digital economy can not only directly narrow the local urban-rural consumption gap, but also narrow the urban-rural consumption gap in neighboring areas more strongly. This study enriches the understanding of the digital economy in narrowing the urban-rural development gap.

title: Digital Transformation and the Ethics of Professional Responsibility: A Maqāṣid Al-Sharī‘Ah Perspective
summary: Digital transformation has reshaped the professional landscape through the increasing use of artificial intelligence, big data, and social media, while simultaneously generating ethical challenges, including technology misuse, privacy violations, and disinformation. This study aims to examine the role of professional codes of ethics in addressing digital ethical challenges through the perspective of maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah. Employing a qualitative approach, the study combines a literature review with case analysis, including the scandal involving the Community Vocational Training Center (Balai Latihan Kerja Komunitas/BLKK) of the Islamic Scholars Association (PP) in Pekalongan City. The findings indicate that professional codes of ethics function not merely as normative instruments governing professional conduct but also as mechanisms for protecting public welfare in accordance with the objectives of maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah, particularly ḥifẓ al-‘aql (protection of intellect), ḥifẓ al-māl (protection of wealth), ḥifẓ al-‘irḍ (protection of dignity), and ḥifẓ al-nafs (protection of life). The implementation of professional codes of ethics through strengthened digital ethics literacy, professional oversight, and technology-responsive regulatory reform can prevent harm, enhance accountability, and sustain public trust. The findings of this study contribute to proposing the integration of professional codes of ethics with maqāṣid al-sharī‘ah as an adaptive ethical framework for strengthening professionalism in the digital era.

title: Investigating The Influence of Digital Transformation, Budgeting and Budgetary Control on The Financial Performance of SMEs: A Critical Review
summary: This critical review evaluates the study by Ebhota et al. (2024) concerning the impact of digital transformation (DGT), big data analytics (BDA), customer experience (CUE), and budgeting and budgetary control (BBC) on the financial performance (FFP) of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in emerging markets. Employing a critical literature review methodology, this paper assesses the original study's theoretical foundations, methodological rigor, and empirical claims. The analysis confirms that grounding the research in Dynamic Capability Theory effectively frames digital transformation as an evolving operational asset rather than a static IT expenditure. Furthermore, the underlying statistical models robustly validate that DGT, BDA, and CUE significantly enhance budgetary controls and financial performance. However, this critical review identifies notable limitations in the original manuscript, including a pronounced demographic sample bias toward highly digitized technology and financial sectors (67%), which limits generalizability to traditional resource-heavy industries, alongside significant typographical and statistical reporting errors in the text. Despite these flaws, the reviewed study offers a highly relevant, empirically backed framework demonstrating how modern SMEs must integrate digital capabilities with financial discipline to achieve sustainable growth

title: Carbon Footprints and Indonesia Market Dynamics: The Risk-Mitigation Role of Artificial Intelligence Innovation
summary: Climate transition has increased investors' concerns about carbon risk, yet evidence remains limited on how firms' technological capabilities shape market responses, particularly in emerging markets. This study examines the effect of carbon risk on stock performance and the moderating role of AI innovation among non financial companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2016 - 2024. Drawing on Asset Pricing Theory, Signaling Theory, and Stakeholder Theory, this study argues that AI innovation reduces investors' uncertainty by enhancing firms' environmental management and signaling stronger technological capability. Indonesia provides a relevant setting because its carbon regulation, sustainability reporting, and AI adoption are still evolving. The results show that carbon risk is marginally associated with lower stock returns and increases stock volatility, while AI innovation significantly weakens the positive effect of carbon risk on stock volatility but has no direct effect on stock returns. This study contributes to the climate finance literature by providing evidence from an emerging market and demonstrating that AI innovation serves as a strategic mechanism for mitigating the financial impact of carbon-transition risk. The findings offer implications for managers, investors, and policymakers in supporting a more resilient low-carbon transition

title: Strategic Information Systems and Digital Capability as Enablers of Digital Transformation in Indonesian Higher Education University
summary: Digital transformation has become an essential strategic initiative for higher education institutions seeking to improve service quality, enhance operational efficiency, and strengthen data-driven governance. Despite the increasing adoption of digital technologies, limited empirical research has examined how Strategic Information Systems (SIS) contribute to Digital Transformation through the development of Digital Capability. This study investigates the relationship between Strategic Information Systems, Digital Capability, and Digital Transformation in the higher education context. An exploratory qualitative case study was conducted at University PGRI Yogyakarta (UPY), Indonesia. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews, observations, organizational documents, and insider inquiry, and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings reveal that Strategic Information Systems serve as key enablers by providing integrated digital infrastructure, facilitating information sharing, and supporting organizational decision-making. These capabilities strengthen Digital Capability, which subsequently drives Digital Transformation across the institution. The study also shows that Digital Capability supports process integration, continuous system enhancement, service innovation, and data-driven governance practices. Informants also reported value creation in academic and administrative services. This research contributes to the Information Systems literature by providing exploratory evidence on the role of Digital Capability in linking Strategic Information Systems with Digital Transformation. The findings offer practical guidance for university leaders and information system managers in developing integrated digital ecosystems that support long-term institutional development.

summary: The development of the green economy in Uzbekistan, its role in ensuring sustainable economic growth, and the interrelationship between environmental and economic processes are examined. Uzbekistan's transition toward a green economy and relevant international experience are also considered, with particular attention to the priority areas of developing green technologies, promoting investment, and ensuring the efficient use of natural resources. The importance of the green economy in integrating economic growth, human well-being, and environmental sustainability is substantiated.

title: Correlação entre as Práticas Ambientais, Sociais e de Governança (ESG) e o Ecoturismo na Gestão de Parques Nacionais Brasileiros
summary: Objetivo – Analisar as práticas ambientais, sociais e de governança (ESG) correlacionadas ao ecoturismo na gestão dos Parques Nacionais (PARNA) brasileiros, sob a perspectiva de seus gestores. Desenho/metodologia/abordagem – A pesquisa adotou abordagem quantitativa, de caráter exploratório e descritivo, utilizando um questionário estruturado (survey) com questões em escala tipo Likert de cinco pontos. O instrumento foi enviado aos 75 gestores dos PARNA brasileiros, obtendo-se 23 respostas válidas. Os dados foram analisados no software MAXQDA por meio da correlação de Spearman entre os critérios de ecoturismo e os eixos ambiental, social e de governança do ESG. Resultados – Os resultados evidenciaram associações positivas entre as práticas de ecoturismo e os três eixos do ESG, com destaque para correlações muito significativas e altamente significativas relacionadas ao eixo ambiental. As análises indicam que práticas de conservação, educação ambiental, governança e participação social podem atuar de forma integrada no fortalecimento do uso público e da gestão dos Parques Nacionais. Implicações práticas – O instrumento desenvolvido apresenta potencial para apoiar o ICMBio na estruturação de uma ferramenta de diagnóstico das práticas ESG nos Parques Nacionais, subsidiando o planejamento, o monitoramento da gestão e a definição de prioridades para o aperfeiçoamento do uso público. Originalidade/valor – O estudo amplia a discussão sobre a aplicação da abordagem ESG em áreas naturais protegidas, um tema ainda pouco explorado na literatura, propondo um instrumento de avaliação aplicável à gestão de Parques Nacionais brasileiros. Limitações da pesquisa – Os resultados refletem exclusivamente a percepção dos gestores participantes e devem ser interpretados considerando a taxa de retorno obtida. Recomenda-se que pesquisas futuras adotem estratégias de triangulação de dados, incorporando a percepção de outros atores envolvidos na gestão e no uso público.

title: GREEN INDUSTRIALISATION AND EXPORT DIVERSIFICATION IN UZBEKISTAN: PATHWAYS TO LOW-CARBON VALUE CHAINS
summary: This article examines how green industrialisation can help Uzbekistan upgrade its export structure and raise foreign-trade earnings as the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) and the scheduled end of GSP+ preferences in 2027 change market-access conditions. The study uses a qualitative, policy-analytic approach: it analyses official strategies and international reports, describes energy, emissions, financial and trade indicators, and assesses policy options against existing capabilities, market access and enabling conditions. It identifies five pathways: clean power and grids, decarbonisation of existing export sectors, upgrading of textiles and agro-processing, new low-carbon products, and green finance based on a national taxonomy. The results suggest that reliable low-carbon electricity should come first, followed by decarbonisation of sectors with existing capabilities, with the period to 2027 as a critical window. The summary lies in linking Uzbekistan's export capabilities, studied earlier mainly through comparative advantage and diversification measures, with green industrial policy and carbon-border requirements in one pathway framework.

title: From Recovery To Sustainability: The Mediating Role of Resilience In Post-Disaster Msmes
summary: This study aims to analyze a model of post-disaster resilience and sustainability of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) based on adaptive capability, risk management, and digital transformation in Langkat Regency. This study employed a quantitative approach using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). The research variables consisted of adaptive capability, risk management, digital transformation, MSME resilience, and MSME sustainability. The results showed that adaptive capability, risk management, and digital transformation had positive and significant effects on MSME resilience, with path coefficients of 0.310, 0.280, and 0.340, respectively. MSME resilience also had a positive and significant effect on MSME sustainability, with a path coefficient of 0.390. Furthermore, all three independent variables had direct and significant effects on MSME sustainability. The mediation analysis indicated that MSME resilience partially mediated the relationships between adaptive capability, risk management, digital transformation, and MSME sustainability. The R² value of 0.624 indicates that the model explains 62.4% of the variance in MSME resilience, while the R² value of 0.687 indicates that 68.7% of the variance in MSME sustainability is explained by the model. These findings confirm that strengthening adaptive capability, risk management, and digital transformation through enhanced resilience is important for supporting the sustainability of post-disaster MSMEs in Langkat Regency.

title: Digital Financial Inclusion and Economic Resilience in Nigeria Amid Geo-economic Fragmentation: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Nigeria is navigating an era of intensifying geo-economic fragmentation, volatile commodity markets, and structural fiscal constraints, even as the digital financial ecosystem has expanded rapidly since 2020. This study adopts the SLR approach, enforced by the PRISMA 2020 reporting guidelines, to synthesise literature between 2020 and 2026 on the relationship between digital Financial Inclusion, financial markets development, and economic resilience in Nigeria. Sixty-one records were initially identified in multiple repositories: after screening for reference duplication and methodological transparency, 31 studies met the inclusive criteria and were thematically analysed. The review finds that mobile money, agent banking, pos platforms and the e-Naira, CBN's digital currency, have measurably expanded the reach of formal financial services participation for previously unbanked and rural populations, but usage inclusion gaps, weak digital literacy and infrastructure deficit continue to constrain the depth of inclusion. It further finds that digital Financial deepening is associated with improved household and firm-level resilience to income and price shocks, and that Nigeria's growing non-oil services -led growth trajectory is particularly attributed to fintech -enabled sectors, such as telecommunications and financial services. The study concludes with policy recommendations that the Nigerian government, CBN and other relevant stakeholders should intensify investment in digital infrastructure. This will help reduce persistent access and usage gaps and promote inclusive participation in the digital financial ecosystem. Government and fintech companies should expand financial and digital literacy programmes, particularly among rural households, women, low-income groups and other financially excluded populations.

title: Air Quality and Emission Trends Following the 2021 Environmental Code Reform in Kazakhstan Across Regions and Industrial Sectors
summary: The 2021 revision of the Environmental Code of the Republic of Kazakhstan was introduced to align with the World Health Organization (WHO) air quality guidelines and the national carbon neutrality strategy for 2060. The revised Code reflects a transformation of environmental governance, including the transition towards a low-carbon and climate-oriented policy framework, the tightening of air quality standards, the strengthening of environmental monitoring, the expansion of region-specific regulatory mechanisms, and increased emphasis on the implementation of Best Available Techniques (BAT). This study presents a comparative analysis of atmospheric pollutant emissions across regions and industrial sectors, including major pollutants such as PM2.5, SO2, CO, NO2, and others. The analysis considers ambient air quality indicators, pollutant composition, the chemical composition of atmospheric precipitation, regional industrial profiles, and changes observed during the reform period. The findings demonstrate substantial regional and pollutant-specific heterogeneity in air-quality dynamics. Although stationary-source emissions decreased by approximately 5–6% between 2021 and 2024, no statistically significant improvement in the assessed ambient-air indicators was identified between 2021 and 2025. Persistent high pollution levels and episodic particulate matter exceedances remained evident in several cities. These findings provide an empirical basis for further assessment of the environmental outcomes of the revised Environmental Code.

title: Is China’s GDP undervalued? A digital economy model
summary: Abstract Transactions in a digital economy generate data that firms accumulate but national accounts do not price. Within the model developed here, that omission implies measured GDP understates output. We adapt the recursive data-economy framework of Farboodi and Veldkamp (2026) to China and construct a bottom-up measure of digital investment from the itemized asset disclosures of 5,120 listed firms. The model does not identify a unique asset perimeter, so we carry two measurement boundaries throughout rather than designating one as the headline. For 2024 the adjustment is 1.60% of GDP, or 2.16 trillion RMB, under a broad boundary that includes telecommunications network assets, and 0.60%, or 0.82 trillion RMB, under a narrow boundary that excludes them. These are alternative measurement boundaries, not statistical bounds. On listed firms alone, before any extrapolation to unlisted firms, the broad-boundary figure is 0.91%. Because the knowledge stock is not identified without forecast-error data, the broad-boundary figure carries a calibrated scenario range of 0.77–4.07%, which reflects alternative calibrations rather than sampling uncertainty. Every figure is conditional on a normalization of the mapping between measured digital investment and the value of data. A validation audit of the classifier uncovers measurement defects that are not specific to China.

title: Mapping the Intersection of Risk-Based Maintenance and Climate Finance: A Scoping Review
summary: The decarbonization of the steel industry requires major investment decisions concerning the continued operation, revamp, or replacement of blast furnace assets. However, these decisions involve not only equipment reliability and maintenance risks but also financial feasibility, climate transition risks, and the potential for stranded assets. The intersection between risk-based maintenance (RBM) and climate finance therefore remains insufficiently explored. This scoping review aims to systematically map the intersection of RBM methodologies and climate finance frameworks and identify asset selection criteria relevant to blast furnace revamp decisions. Following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, the review synthesizes 47 studies across three thematic domains: risk-based maintenance approaches, climate finance mechanisms, and steel industry decarbonization pathways. The review reveals a critical gap in integrated decision-making frameworks that simultaneously address equipment reliability, financial viability, and climate transition risk. Key criteria identified include technology readiness levels, carbon abatement costs, stranded asset risks, and green finance eligibility. These findings provide a foundation for practitioners and policymakers to integrate asset management, capital investment, and climate finance considerations when making strategic blast furnace decisions aligned with long-term climate neutrality objectives.

title: Talent Mobility dalam Ekosistem Digital
summary: Digital transformation has changed the way organizations manage human resources, including in the areas of acquiring, developing, retaining, and mobilizing talent. In this context, talent mobility is no longer limited to employee transfers but also encompasses career mobility, knowledge transfer, competency development, and the adaptation of talent to the organization’s increasingly dynamic needs. This study aims to analyze the development of research on talent mobility within the digital ecosystem and to identify patterns of findings, methodological approaches, and key themes emerging in the literature. The study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach, involving a systematic process of literature identification, selection, extraction, and synthesis based on predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria. The results of the study indicate that talent mobility is evolving at the intersection of talent management, digital transformation, competency development, career mobility, artificial intelligence, and digital talent management. The literature also highlights the increasing use of digital technologies in competency mapping, career development, recruitment, training, retention, and talent needs planning. This study contributes by integrating the perspectives of talent mobility and digital transformation and provides a conceptual foundation for organizations to develop adaptive, data-driven talent management systems.

title: Behavioral Heterogeneity and the Evolution of Financial Decision-Making in Contemporary Markets
summary: This paper examines the relationship between investor behavior, market volatility, and financial decision-making by synthesizing recent contributions from behavioral finance, household finance, market microstructure, sustainable investment, and digital finance. The literature shows that financial decisions cannot be explained exclusively by conventional assumptions of rational expectations and efficient information processing. Investor sentiment, attention, risk perception, overconfidence, personal experience, social interaction, and financial literacy influence portfolio allocation, market participation, and responses to uncertainty. These behavioral mechanisms also contribute to market volatility by affecting trading intensity, herding, disagreement, and reactions to economic or policy shocks. The development of digital trading platforms, social media, crowdfunding, FinTech, and blockchain further modifies the channels through which investors receive information and make financial choices. At the same time, environmental and sustainability preferences increasingly influence portfolio construction and asset pricing. The literature therefore suggests that financial outcomes result from interactions among economic fundamentals, behavioral characteristics, information structures, institutional conditions, and technological change. Understanding these relationships provides a broader framework for explaining heterogeneous investment decisions and short-term market fluctuations.

This study synthesizes how the competency-strategy matrix is transformed in the digital era. A systematic literature review (SLR) following PRISMA 2020 was applied to journal articles from Google Scholar, Garuda, Neliti, and Scopus. The matrix evolves through administrative, strategy-linked, and digitally adaptive stages. Digital transformation shifts competency demands toward digital, data, and behavioral skills, while technologies such as enterprise systems and artificial intelligence bring efficiency but also the risk of dehumanization. The study proposes an integrative framework and a research agenda.
