title: FROM COSMIC INDEBTEDNESS TO STATUTORY CORPORATE BENEVOLENCE: RE-ENVISIONING INDIA'S LEGAL MANDATE OF CORPORATE PHILANTHROPY AS AN ECHO OF THE ANCIENT TRADITION OF DHARMA: A STUDY OF SELECTED INDIAN CORPORATIONS
summary: The 21st century has witnessed an unprecedented transformation in the philosophy of corporate governance. Business organisations are no longer perceived merely as institutions for generating economic wealth; rather, they are increasingly expected to function as custodians of social welfare, environmental sustainability, ethical governance, and inclusive development. This transition has acquired legal recognition in India through the enactment of Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, making corporate social responsibility (CSR) expenditure mandatory for eligible companies. Although this statutory obligation is generally viewed as a contemporary legal innovation, the philosophical foundations of corporate philanthropy have existed in Indian civilisation for several millennia. Ancient Indian scriptures consistently propounded that every individual and institution exists within an interconnected cosmic order and is therefore indebted to society, nature, knowledge traditions, ancestors, and the Divine. This philosophy, popularly known as the doctrine of Pancha Ṛiṇ (Five Cosmic Debts), constitutes one of the earliest ethical frameworks advocating responsible utilisation and redistribution of resources. Unlike modern legal compliance, these obligations were internalised as Dharma, a voluntary moral commitment arising from gratitude towards the universe. The present study attempts to establish that the contemporary statutory framework governing Corporate Social Responsibility in India represents not merely a legal innovation but a modern institutional manifestation of an ancient civilisational ethos. Drawing upon the Bhagavad Geeta, the Upanishads, Manusmriti, Mahabharata, and other classical Indian philosophical texts, this paper analyses the ethical foundations of philanthropic responsibility and compares them with the objectives underlying mandatory CSR under the Companies Act, 2013. Particular emphasis is placed on the doctrine of Pancha Ṛiṇ and its remarkable correspondence with present-day corporate obligations relating to education, healthcare, environmental conservation, rural development, community welfare, and sustainable economic growth. The empirical component of the study examines CSR initiatives undertaken by five leading Indian corporations representing diverse industrial sectors: Tata Steel Limited, Infosys Limited, Reliance Industries Limited, ITC Limited, and Mahindra & Mahindra Limited. Through qualitative comparative analysis based on publicly available sustainability reports and statutory disclosures, the paper identifies significant similarities between ancient Indian ethical philosophy and modern corporate governance while simultaneously recognising important areas where contemporary CSR has evolved beyond traditional frameworks, particularly in matters concerning gender equity, climate governance, digital inclusion, stakeholder accountability, and regulatory compliance. The study argues that India’s CSR legislation possesses a distinctive philosophical identity because it resonates with indigenous ethical traditions rather than merely borrowing Western stakeholder theories. Consequently, statutory corporate philanthropy may be interpreted as a revival of India's ancient doctrine of cosmic responsibility adapted to contemporary socio-economic realities. Such an interpretation aligns profoundly with the vision articulated in the Seventh Chapter of the Asian Integration Forum, which envisages a borderless world founded upon equality, fraternity, liberty, ecological harmony, and collective human prosperity. The paper concludes that integrating ancient wisdom with modern corporate governance offers a sustainable pathway towards inclusive development, ethical capitalism, and global human welfare.

title: From Compliance to Conscience: Evaluating the Efficacy of ESG Regulations in India's Climate Governance
summary: Global discussions about sustainability in life revolve around changing human mindsets while legal frameworks focus on changing reporting systems.This paper contends that the current ESG regulatory framework in India, which SEBI Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) is a part of, is at risk of imposing a culture of mere compliance to checklists rather than real corporate climate accountability.The main aim of the study is to assess the functioning of Companies Act, 2013 and the recent SEBI regulations on the belief that the laws many observers feel are largely reactive mechanisms for compliance than proactive tools for environmental stewardship.The paper adopts a doctrinal and analytical approach, examining the gap that exists in between the policy objectives of ESG obligations and actual practices in Indian corporate offices.Specific regulatory barriers are described because they enable business organizations to appear as acting in favor of the environment without changing the very nature of their business.The results show that while India has a high-level reporting scheme, there is a lack of educational system and incentive systems to integrate sustainability into the legal framework.For ESG laws to effectively reshape the planet, it is important for the legal structure to move beyond such governance which is merely based on disclosures.Liability rules ought to be implemented, thereby punishing environmental negligence and rewarding practical climate action, which will narrow the gap between the legal system and conscience of business.

title: FROM DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION TO ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: A NEW PARADIGM OF GLOBAL JOURNALISM
summary: The contemporary media industry is undergoing one of the most profound transformations in the history of mass communication. Digital platforms, social networks, mobile technologies, big data, algorithmic distribution systems and, most recently, generative artificial intelligence have fundamentally changed the production, distribution and consumption of information. The traditional model in which professional media institutions controlled the principal channels of information has evolved into a complex digital ecosystem where journalists, media organisations, technology platforms, bloggers, influencers, artificial intelligence systems and ordinary users simultaneously participate in the creation and circulation of content. This article examines the transformation of mass media in the context of digitalisation, technological innovation and the rapid development of artificial intelligence. Particular attention is paid to the integration of generative AI into newsroom processes, including information gathering, transcription, translation, data analysis, content production, fact-checking, personalisation and audience engagement. The study argues that artificial intelligence should not be interpreted merely as an instrument of automation. Rather, it represents a structural factor capable of changing journalistic workflows, professional competencies, editorial responsibility, media economics and the relationship between media institutions and their audiences. At the same time, AI-driven journalism generates significant professional and ethical risks, including algorithmic bias, hallucinated information, deepfakes, synthetic content, copyright disputes and the possible erosion of public trust. The article concludes that the future competitiveness and social legitimacy of media organisations will depend not simply on technological adoption, but on their ability to combine innovation with professional standards, human editorial oversight, transparency and accountability.

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on the Performance of Islamic Banks in the Gulf Cooperation Council Countries
summary: This research aims to examine the relationship between digital transformation and the performance of 25 Islamic banks in the Gulf Cooperation Council countries over the 2015-2023 period using the Panel-ARDL model and relying on the descriptive approach. The main independent variable is the Digital Transformation Index, in addition to the cost-toincome ratio, the total asset, the deposit-to-asset ratio, the real GDP, and the inflation rate. Return on equity (ROE) is the main performance measure. The study concludes that digital transformation in Islamic banks in the GCC countries is in its early stages, but it is increasing following the Corona pandemic crisis in 2020. The study found a significant positive relationship between the return on equity and the digital transformation index in Islamic banks in the long terms, so greater investment in digital transformation leads to improved performance. The cost-to-income ratio, the total asset, and the inflation rate have a negative significant impact on the performance of Islamic banks. Real GDP has shown a significant positive impact on ROE, and the deposit-to-asset ratio has no significant impact on the ROE. The researchers recommended that Islamic banks should continue their digital transformation efforts, with the necessity of adopting advanced digital technologies to reduce costs and increase performance.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF THE RUSSIAN OIL AND GAS INDUSTRY: RISK ASSESSMENT AND DEVELOPMENT POTENTIAL
summary: Digitalization of Russia’s oil and gas industry serves as a key driver of resilience and competitiveness under the pressures of the energy transition, sanctions, and the need for technological sovereignty. This study aims to assess the current level of digital maturity in the Russian oil and gas sector and to identify the main risks and opportunities associated with digital transformation.The author uses content analysis of strategic and corporate documents, comparative analysis of indicators of digital activity of leading companies and integral indexing to assess digital maturity. This approach allows us to compare the dynamics of digital investments and the scale of adoption of end-to-end technologies.The analysis shows that the major oil and gas companies are consistently increasing digital investments and expanding the use of digital deposits, digital twins, IoT and artificial intelligence. At the same time, the level of digital maturity remains uneven, and the effects of digitalization often appear fragmented. The study identifies key risk groups, including technological, cyber, institutional, and workforce-related risks.The author interprets digital transformation as an integrated organizational and economic process, rather than a set of individual IT projects. The paper outlines directions for improving digitalization efficiency, including the development of digital maturity metrics, the adaptation of strategic planning to a data-driven model, and the strengthening of business analytics in the management of Russia’s oil and gas industry.

title: Pengaruh Kepemilikan Manajerial dan Kepemilikan Institusional terhadap Audit Report Lag: Studi Empiris Pada Perusahaan Sektor Energi yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: Late publication of audited financial statements remains a persistent problem in Indonesia's capital market and is especially relevant in the energy sector, where capital-intensive operations and exposure to commodity price and policy shocks make audits more complex. Evidence on whether ownership structure shortens audit report lag is inconsistent across countries and sectors, and few studies have tested it in this sector. Drawing on agency theory, managerial ownership (an alignment mechanism) and institutional ownership (a monitoring mechanism) are tested as determinants of audit report lag, with firm size, profitability, leverage, and auditor type as controls. Multiple linear regression is applied to 140 firm-year observations from 28 energy-sector firms listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024, with extreme audit report lag values winsorized to address non-normality. Neither managerial ownership nor institutional ownership has a significant partial effect on audit report lag, whereas higher profitability and engagement of a Big Four auditor are associated with shorter lag. The model explains only a limited share of the variation in audit report lag, so the results are best read as associations within this sample rather than conclusive evidence. The study contributes evidence from a capital-intensive, rarely examined sector showing that ownership structure alone does not account for reporting timeliness, while profitability and auditor characteristics appear more relevant.

title: Trends in 21st-Century Learning Technology Research: Digital Transformation, AI, and Adaptive Learning
summary: The rapid evolution of digital technologies, artificial intelligence (AI), and adaptive learning is reshaping 21st-century education, yet their interrelationships and research trajectories remain fragmented. This study systematically reviews research published from 2020 to 2026 to examine the evolution, dominant and emerging themes, and conceptual relationships across digital transformation, AI, and adaptive learning. Using a systematic literature review with thematic synthesis, relevant studies were analyzed temporally and thematically to identify shifts in research orientation and emerging directions. The findings reveal a progressive transition from technology integration and digital learning environments toward intelligent tutoring, personalization, adaptive learning, and, more recently, generative AI and human–AI collaboration. Conceptually, digital transformation functions as the enabling ecosystem, AI as an intelligent capability, and adaptive learning as a learner-responsive application. Importantly, AI-enabled personalization does not necessarily constitute adaptive learning; meaningful adaptation requires continuous responsiveness to learner performance, needs, feedback, and learning trajectories. The synthesis further indicates that technological advancement alone is insufficient, highlighting teacher agency, learner autonomy, organizational readiness, data governance, and ethical accountability. The study proposes a human-centered and responsible orientation in which AI augments pedagogical judgment rather than displacing it.

title: Materiality Never Settles: Why Mandatory Sustainability Reporting Requires Continuous ESG Governance
summary: The Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) are widely expected to reduce ambiguity in corporate sustainability reporting by standardizing how organizations identify and disclose material issues. This Perspective challenges that expectation. Informed by findings from a prior empirical study of Austrian regional state-owned hospitals, we argue that mandatory sustainability reporting does not eliminate organizational uncertainty but transforms it into an ongoing governance challenge. Rather than producing a stable set of material issues, double materiality assessments require organizations to continuously interpret, negotiate, and revise sustainability priorities as regulatory expectations, climate risks, and stakeholder demands evolve. This reframes double materiality from a one-off compliance exercise into a recurring organizational capability, extending prior accounts of materiality as contested and negotiated by showing that mandatory regulation institutionalizes this contestation as a standing governance task rather than resolving it. Building on institutional theory and sensemaking research, we conceptualize this as a continuous ESG governance cycle rather than a linear compliance process. The effectiveness of future sustainability reporting may depend not only on increasingly sophisticated reporting standards, but also on organizations’ capacity to govern the uncertainty inherent in evolving materiality judgements, with direct implications for materiality assessment in public-sector and healthcare organizations.

title: Governing Digital Benefit Claims Over Time: Evidential, Operational and Temporal Assurance for Digital Transformation
summary: The proposed method treats each benefit claim as a persistent, configuration-dependent evidential object. Claim states are proposition-relative: they apply to a specified magnitude, scope, population or workflow, configuration and decision context. Claims are assessed through evidential validity, operational conversion and temporal validity and carry one of four states: Proposed, Validated, Qualified or Suspended. Configuration change triggers qualification only when it is plausibly material to evidence supporting the proposition, or when a predetermined revalidation threshold is reached. The method's candidate contribution is the explicit connection between current evidential standing and the governance treatment of individual benefit assertions. Its distinctiveness should be retained only if it identifies unsupported current assertions earlier or more reliably than competent conventional benefits governance at acceptable burden. title: Rare Earth Element Recycling for Sustainable Energy Storage and Renewable Technology Supply Chains: A Critical Review with ASEAN Perspectives
summary: The global shift toward renewable energy and electrified transport has sharply increased demand for rare earth elements (REEs), particularly neodymium, praseodymium, and dysprosium used in NdFeB permanent magnets for wind turbines and electric vehicle motors, yet recycling currently supplies only a small share of this demand. This paper presents a critical review of REE recycling technologies for NdFeB magnet waste, benchmarking hydrometallurgical, short-loop, pyrometallurgical, and emerging bioleaching routes against recovery efficiency, purity, cost profile, and environmental footprint. The review situates these findings within ASEAN's position in the global critical minerals value chain, examining the region's reserve base, processing infrastructure, and exposure to supply concentration. Findings are then mapped against all seven programme areas of the ASEAN Plan of Action for Energy Cooperation (APAEC) 2026-2030, and research gaps are identified across techno-economic data availability, process scale-up, and regional policy coordination. The paper concludes with proposed directions for coordinated ASEAN investment in recycling infrastructure, aligned with the region's Just and Inclusive Energy Transition goal.

title: Improving Organisational And Economic Mechanisms For Sustainable Energy Efficiency Gains In Service Enterprises On The Basis Of Digital Transformation And Innovative Management Technologies
summary: Service enterprises such as hotels, retail outlets and restaurants account for a growing share of electricity demand in emerging economies, yet energy efficiency in this segment is usually pursued through isolated equipment replacements rather than through a managed, continuously improving system. This article develops and tests an improved organisational and economic mechanism that integrates an ISO 50001-based energy management system, digital monitoring and control technologies, a cost-of-saved-energy decision rule and energy performance contracting. The mechanism is applied to an illustrative portfolio of three service enterprises in Uzbekistan with a combined baseline consumption of 4,170 MWh per year, evaluated at the electricity tariff for legal entities of 1,100 soums per kWh in force from 1 June 2026. Seven measures reduce consumption by 1,490.9 MWh, or 35.8%, require 4,860 million soums of investment, pay back in 3.3 years on average and generate a net present value of 2,552.8 million soums at a 16% discount rate. Digital and managerial measures deliver 39.4% of total savings. A marginal cost curve shows that all measures have a levelised cost of saved energy below the tariff, ranging from 410 to 1,035 soums per kWh, while the portfolio remains profitable down to a tariff of 754 soums per kWh. An energy performance contract under which a service company retains 75% of verified savings for 10 years yields the investor an internal rate of return of 17.8% and leaves the client 410 million soums per year from the first year without capital outlay. The results show that sustainable efficiency gains depend less on individual technologies than on combining measurement, management routines and financing in one mechanism.

title: AI & Data-Driven Inventory Management for Improving Medicine Availability at Jan Aushadhi Kendras
summary: Abstract: The rapid expansion of the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) has significantly enhanced access to affordable generic medicines across India through a growing network of Jan Aushadhi Kendras (JAKs). However, the long-term success of this network relies heavily on consistent medicine availability. Operational challenges—such as localized stockouts, inventory imbalances, and expiry-related wastage—disrupt supply chains and threaten patient access to affordable healthcare. This highlights a critical need to examine how emerging tools like Artificial Intelligence (AI) and predictive data analytics can optimize inventory management within the PMBJP framework. The purpose of this study is to examine the potential of AI-based demand forecasting and data-driven inventory models to maximize medicine availability and improve asset turnover at JAKs. The study adopts a descriptive and analytical research design based on secondary data sourced from PMBI and PIB publications, government reports, and peer-reviewed literature on AI applications in pharmaceutical logistics. Trend analysis, comparative evaluations, and qualitative synthesis are utilized to assess PMBJP’s unique operating environment against empirical evidence from comparable health systems. Findings from parallel healthcare settings show that AI-enabled inventory systems can reduce stockouts by 30–55%, increase inventory turnover by up to 70%, and cut expired inventory losses by 20–33%. While these figures do not represent direct empirical data from individual JAK outlets, they provide robust conceptual support for AI integration. Crucially, the study identifies PMBI’s existing IT-enabled supply chain infrastructure and digital ecosystem as an ideal, mature foundation to host these future AI applications. Future research should focus on developing and testing JAK-specific AI models using store-level sales, inventory, and localized demand data. Implementing such automated decision-support models could systematically eliminate stockouts, curb chemical wastage, and strengthen overall supply chain resilience. Ultimately, this technological transition supports more reliable public access to affordable medicines, contributing directly to a highly inclusive and sustainable public healthcare system. summary: ملخص البحث عيون لا تنام: كيف توظّف إسرائيل الكاميرات والطائرات المسيّرة وبرامج التجسس للسيطرة على الفلسطينيين الباحث: نور الدين وائل عبدالله عرجانالتخصص: الأمن السيبراني والذكاء الاصطناعي والتحقيقات الرقمية يتناول هذا البحث توظيف تقنيات المراقبة الرقمية في السياق الفلسطيني، مع التركيز على أنظمة التعرف على الوجوه، والطائرات المسيّرة، وبرامج التجسس المتقدمة، وانعكاساتها على الخصوصية والحقوق الرقمية وحرية الحركة والأمن الإنساني. ويهدف إلى تحليل الأدلة المنشورة المتعلقة بهذه التقنيات، وتقييم مدى موثوقيتها، والتمييز بين الاستخدامات التي تدعمها تقارير حقوقية وفحوص تقنية مستقلة، والقدرات الممكنة من الناحية العلمية التي لا يتوافر دليل منشور كافٍ لإثبات استخدامها في حالات فلسطينية محددة. يعتمد البحث على منهج تحليلي نوعي قائم على مراجعة المصادر المفتوحة، بما يشمل تقارير المنظمات الحقوقية، والتحقيقات الصحفية، والدراسات الأكاديمية، والتقارير التقنية المتخصصة. ويستعرض نماذج من استخدام أنظمة التعرف على الوجوه في الخليل والقدس الشرقية، وحالات اختراق هواتف مدافعين فلسطينيين عن حقوق الإنسان باستخدام برنامج التجسس «بيغاسوس»، إلى جانب تحليل القدرات التقنية المحتملة للطائرات المسيّرة في الرصد والاستطلاع والحرب الإلكترونية، مع مراعاة حدود الأدلة المتاحة بشأن كل قدرة. ويخلص البحث إلى أن المراقبة الرقمية لا تقتصر آثارها على جمع البيانات، بل قد تمتد إلى تقييد الحركة، وإضعاف الخصوصية، وتعزيز الشعور بالمراقبة المستمرة، وإحداث آثار محتملة على حرية التعبير والعمل الحقوقي. كما يؤكد أهمية الفصل بين إثبات وقوع الاختراق وإسناده إلى جهة محددة، وبين إثبات القدرة التقنية وإثبات استخدامها الفعلي. ويوصي بتعزيز التحقيقات الرقمية المستقلة، وتطوير آليات الرقابة والمساءلة، وحماية البيانات البيومترية، وتمكين الأفراد والمؤسسات الفلسطينية من أدوات الأمن الرقمي والتحقق التقني. يسهم هذا البحث في تقديم قراءة تحليلية تربط بين الأمن السيبراني وحقوق الإنسان والتحقيقات الرقمية، وتدعو إلى تقييم تقنيات المراقبة في السياقات الخاضعة للاحتلال استنادًا إلى الأدلة المنشورة، والدقة المنهجية، ومبادئ المساءلة وحماية الحقوق الأساسية.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION MANAGEMENT IN ISLAMIC EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS: ADAPTATION STRATEGIES FOR THE ERA OF THE INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION 4.0 AND 5.0
summary: Digital transformation is both a challenge and an opportunity for Islamic educational institutions in facing the dynamics of the Industrial Revolution 4.0 and Society 5.0. This study aims to analyze the digital transformation management strategies implemented by Islamic educational institutions in improving the effectiveness of governance and learning quality. The research method used is a qualitative approach with the library research method, which is by examining various literature and the latest research results that are relevant to the topic of digital transformation and Islamic education management. The results of the study show that the success of digital transformation is determined by three main aspects, namely visionary leadership based on Islamic values, strengthening the digital literacy of educators and education personnel, and integrating information technology systems in the management of educational institutions. In addition, it was found that Islamic educational institutions that are able to adapt strategically to technological changes have higher competitiveness in creating an effective, innovative, and characterful learning ecosystem. The conclusion of this study emphasizes the importance of synergy between spiritual values and technological innovation in realizing globally competitive Islamic education in the digital era.

title: Strategi Peningkatan Sustainable Supply Chain Performance Pada Perusahaan Remanufaktur Melalui Sustainable Value Stream Mapping (Sus-VSM)
summary: Persaingan global memerlukan strategi yang tidak hanya bertumpu pada efisiensi, tetapi juga harus memperhatikan aspek lingkungan. Remanufaktur sebagai bagian dari ekonomi sirkular menjadi solusi strategis melalui pengurangan limbah, penghematan sumber daya dan pelestarian nilai produk. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengevaluasi kinerja SSCM di PT Komatsu Remanufacturing Asia (P.T KRA) menggunakan metode Sustainable Value Stream Mapping (Sus-VSM) yang terintegrasi dengan Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP). Untuk memastikan proses penelitian didukung oleh data yang valid, maka pada penelitian ini pengumpulan data dilakukan melalui observasi langsung, wawancara, serta pengumpulan data primer dan sekunder. Perancangan Metrik pengukuran keberlanjutan dikembangkan berdasarkan kajian literatur dan divalidasi menggunakan pengujian konstansi, validitas dan reliabilitas. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa kinerja SSCM perusahaan P.T KRA berada pada kategori cukup baik (Moderately Good) dengan nilai indeks keberlanjutan sebesar 77. Dimensi lingkungan dan sosial menunjukkan kinerja yang relatif kuat, akan tetapi dimensi ekonomi masih memerlukan perbaikan, khususnya pada pengurangan lead time, peningkatan overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), efisiensi penggunaan air dan pengelolaan limbah padat. Temuan ini menegaskan pentingnya Sus-VSM sebagai alat evaluasi komprehensif untuk mendukung peningkatan efisiensi secara berkelanjutan dalam rantai pasok remanufaktur.

title: Building capacity for short food supply chains through food processing workshops: Experience from the Horizon Europe RURBANIVE project
summary: Background Short food supply chains (SFSCs) are increasingly recognised as a means of improving the sustainability, resilience and economic viability of local food systems. However, many farmers and small-scale food producers lack the technological knowledge required to develop value-added products for direct sale. The Horizon Europe RURBANIVE project addresses these challenges through knowledge exchange, capacity building and innovation. Within this framework, practical food processing workshops were designed as multi-actor learning activities promoting collaboration between academia, farmers, food producers and public authorities and building their capacities. This study evaluated participants’ perceptions of the workshops and the potential contribution of those practical courses and digital learning platform for shortening the food supply chains. Methods Between 2025 and 2026, eight practical workshops on dairy, bakery, meat and brewing technologies were organised at the Czech University of Life Sciences Prague. The workshops combined theoretical lectures with hands-on demonstrations on pilot-scale processing lines. Overall, 122stakeholders participated, but only 92 (75.4%) of them completed an anonymous post-workshop questionnaire evaluating nine aspects of the educational activities. Digital learning platform Moodle has been developed as a follow-up of the workshops but cannot be evaluated yet. Results Participant satisfaction was very high. Almost all respondents were satisfied with the workshops, considered the objectives clear and highly rated the facilitators. The duration of the workshops and the balance between theory and practice were positively evaluated, while 77.2% of respondents expressed interest in attending similar events in the future. The workshops resulted in the development of digital learning platform with four production courses and one product marketing course. Conclusions Practical workshops effectively supported knowledge transfer and strengthened participants’ capacity to develop value-added products suitable for direct sales channels. Combined with digital learning tool, they provide a transferable model for supporting short food supply chains and more resilient local food systems.

title: A Review on Pharmaceutical Marketing and Management
summary: Pharmaceutical marketing and management occupy a distinct position among commercial disciplines because they operate at the intersection of profit-driven business objectives and public health responsibility. Thisreview examinesthe strategic, operational, and ethical dimensions of pharma marketing and management, drawing on recent literature covering promotional practices, digital transformation, supply chain operations, and regulatory oversight. The review finds that traditional promotional tools such as medical representative (MR) visits, free drug samples, and continuing medical education (CME) sponsorships remain influential in shaping physician prescribing behaviour, even as digital channels, artificial intelligence (AI), and data analytics increasingly reshape how companies engage healthcare professionals (HCPs) and patients. On the management side, the Indian pharmaceutical supply chain continues to face structural challenges including fragmentation, import dependence on active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), cold chain limitations, and counterfeit products, even as digital tools and regulatory reforms attempt to close these gaps. Ethical concerns persist around inducements, exaggerated promotional claims, and inconsistent enforcement of codes such as the Uniform Code for Pharmaceutical Marketing Practices (UCPMP), which became legally binding in 2024. The review concludes that a balanced, ethically anchored, and technologically integrated approach to marketing and supply chain management is essential for the pharmaceutical sector to serve both commercial and public health goals sustainably.

title: DIGITAL INTELLIGENCE, ETHICAL AI GOVERNANCE, AND HUMAN INTELLIGENCE: A CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR RESPONSIBLE DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN ASIAN COUNTRIES
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI), big data analytics, and cloud computing are accelerating digital transformation by improving organizational efficiency, innovation, and data-driven decision-making across Asian economies. While these technologies create significant opportunities for economic and social development, they also introduce complex ethical challenges, including concerns related to privacy, algorithmic bias, transparency, accountability, cybersecurity, and responsible governance. This conceptual paper proposes a human-centred framework that integrates digital intelligence, ethical AI governance, and human intelligence to support responsible digital transformation. Grounded in the resource-based view, dynamic capability theory, stakeholder theory, institutional theory, and socio-technical systems theory, the framework explains how technological capabilities, ethical governance mechanisms, and human competencies collectively contribute to sustainable organizational performance. This paper emphasises that ethical decision-making, creativity, critical thinking, and responsible leadership remain essential complements to AI-driven systems. By presenting an integrated conceptual perspective, this study offers theoretical insights for future research and practical guidance for policymakers, organizational leaders, and technology practitioners seeking to balance digital innovation with ethical responsibility and long-term societal well-being.

title: Digital transformation of health licensing services: a qualitative study of service processes, human resource capacity, and system reliability in indonesia
summary: ntroduction: Digital transformation has improved the accessibility, transparency, and efficiency of public licensing services. However, health licensing remains dependent on effective procedures, competent personnel, and reliable digital systems. This study explored health licensing services at the Makassar City Investment and One-Stop Integrated Services Agency, focusing on service processes, human resources, and technology. Methods: A descriptive qualitative study was conducted in July 2026. Five informants were selected purposively, comprising one key informant, three primary informants, and one supporting informant. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, non-participant observation, and documentation. The data were organized, reduced, categorized, and interpreted using content analysis, with source, method, and data triangulation applied to strengthen credibility. Results: Licensing procedures generally followed established SOPs, although incomplete documents and limited applicant understanding sometimes caused delays. Personnel demonstrated adequate procedural and communication skills, but workloads increased during peak demand. Digital systems supported service delivery, although slow performance, maintenance, and server downtime occasionally disrupted operations. Conclusion: Health licensing services were generally well implemented, but service quality could be strengthened through clearer applicant information, continuous workforce development, workload management, and improved reliability of digital infrastructure. These improvements may support more accessible, efficient, and resilient public licensing services.

title: K-REAP Digital Transformation: A Kerala Model for Sustainable Enterprise Resource Planning in Large-scale Higher Education Systems
summary: Digital transformation has become a strategic priority for higher education systems worldwide, yet large-scale enterprise resource planning (ERP) implementation remains one of the most challenging institutional reforms. Universities differ substantially in governance structures, academic regulations, examination processes, financial management systems and administrative workflows, complicating the deployment of a unified ERP. Kerala’s Resources for Educational Administration and Planning (K-REAP) project provides a unique opportunity to examine various ERP implementation models over more than a decade of policy experimentation. This article analyzes the evolution of ERP development strategies adopted in Kerala between 2013 and 2026, identifying the factors influencing their success and failure. Four implementation models are examined: centralized software development, integration of existing university applications, institution-owned ERP systems and software-as-a-service (SaaS)-based configurable ERP architecture implemented through K-REAP. Drawing on implementation experience across multiple universities, the study argues that a cloud-hosted, configurable SaaS architecture—supported by multi-level governance, centralized project management, distributed technical teams and vendor-supported continuous customization—offers a more sustainable approach than institution-owned ERP systems. The article proposes a higher education ERP deployment framework that may serve as a reference model for higher education systems implementing digital transformation at scale.

title: Does ESG protect profitability in a crisis? Evidence from US industrial firms during COVID-19
summary: Using the COVID-19 pandemic as a common macroeconomic shock to which firms were differentially exposed, we investigate whether pre-crisis environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance was associated with corporate financial resilience, measured through return on assets (ROA). Two competing directional hypotheses are evaluated: the insurance-value hypothesis (H1a), under which accumulated stakeholder trust protects profitability in crises, and the short-run cost hypothesis (H1b), under which relatively rigid ESG-related commitments depress accounting returns when demand contracts. Using a panel of 70 US industrial firms over 2012–2021 (690 firm-year observations), a two-way fixed-effects (TWFE) difference-in-differences (DiD) framework compares changes in ROA across firms with stronger versus weaker pre-crisis ESG performance. The results are consistent with the short-run cost hypothesis: a one-standard-deviation higher pre-crisis ESG score is associated with an approximately 1.06 percentage-point larger relative decline in crisis-period ROA (continuous specification, p = 0.006), and high-ESG firms experienced a 1.97 percentage-point relative decline compared to low-ESG counterparts (p = 0.019; 95% confidence interval (CI) = −3.60 to −0.33; N = 70 firms), approximately 24% of mean ROA. Dynamic event-study estimates show no differential pre-trends and significant high-ESG differentials in both 2020 and 2021; the penalty is unchanged by controls for research-and-development (R&D) and advertising intensity, is imprecisely larger in the most pandemic-exposed industries in a triple-difference specification, and is attenuated within industry-by-year cells. Pillar-level estimates are precision-limited nulls. Where included, financial leverage is the strongest single predictor of crisis-period profitability. The findings are interpreted through a sustainability trade-off mechanism in which environmental and social commitments behave like fixed capacity investments that build relational value over the long run but increase operating leverage in the short run; they identify a robust profitability pattern consistent with this mechanism, rather than a direct evaluation of it, and caution against treating ESG ratings as guarantees of short-run accounting resilience.

title: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) is a strategic pathway to sustainable competitive advantage
summary: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) frameworks are increasingly recognised, not just as instruments for compliance but also as a strategy for sustainable competitive advantage. Though this is a progressive development, there are identifiable gaps in the research that views ESG as a valuable, rare, inimitable and organised tool for business sustainability and not just a compliance obligation. This research examines the strategic significance of ESG frameworks in improving business sustainability and competitiveness across various countries. The data used in the research are mainly secondary data, and a qualitative comparative approach was applied. The secondary data used were sourced from corporations’ public disclosures, regulatory policies and ESG performance reports in the United Kingdom, the United States and Nigeria. The research focuses on the integration of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) concepts within organisations’ everyday governance structures and corporate responsibility. The study indicates that organisations that deliberately implement ESG frameworks are more successful in securing investors’ trust, customers’ loyalty and employees’ commitments while upscaling regulatory compliance. The research discovered that ESG frameworks are not without challenges, mainly the lack of uniform regulations across jurisdictions. Even within the same jurisdiction, there are different frameworks, and the disparity has made comparative research complex. Despite these issues, companies that diligently and consistently implement ESG frameworks foster innovation, ethical governance and value creation to gain a competitive advantage over counterparts in the same industry.

title: TITLE: IMPROVING MECHANISMS FOR FINANCING ESG-BASED INVESTMENTS IN THE BANKING SECTOR OF UZBEKISTAN
summary: In the context of global economic transformation, the integration of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles has emerged as a fundamental requirement for financial stability and international competitiveness. This research examines the structural and functional mechanisms of ESG-based investment financing within the commercial banking sector of Uzbekistan. As the nation intensifies its transition toward a "Green Economy," financial institutions are tasked with aligning their lending portfolios with sustainable development goals. Through a comprehensive analysis of current regulatory frameworks and the adoption of "Green" banking products, this study evaluates the readiness of the domestic banking sector to implement international sustainability standards. The research identifies critical bottlenecks, such as the lack of a comprehensive national ESG taxonomy, insufficient technical expertise in environmental risk assessment, and limited domestic demand for sustainable financial instruments. The findings propose a systemic model for enhancing ESG financing, emphasizing the development of green bond frameworks, the institutionalization of ESG risk management systems, and the implementation of standardized sustainability reporting. Ultimately, this paper provides strategic recommendations for the Central Bank and commercial lenders to foster a more resilient, transparent, and climate-aligned financial ecosystem in Uzbekistan.

title: The Search for a Universal ESG–FDI Relationship: Why Development and Investment Context Matter
summary: ABSTRACT The empirical literature has not established a consistent relationship between environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance and foreign direct investment (FDI). One reason may be that the association varies with countries' level of development and the structure of their investment flows. This study examines this possibility using a balanced panel of 10 upper‐middle‐income and 10 high‐income economies over the period 2002–2023. The baseline estimates are obtained from country fixed‐effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and are supplemented by lagged and dynamic specifications, pillar‐level analyses, nonlinear models, income–group interactions, and country‐level sensitivity checks. The results point to a negative and statistically significant association between ESG performance and FDI inflows in upper‐middle‐income economies, and this finding is relatively stable across alternative specifications. For high‐income economies, however, the estimates are considerably more sensitive to the composition of the sample. The ESG dimensions also exhibit distinct patterns across the two income groups, suggesting that the aggregate ESG measure masks important underlying heterogeneity. The interaction estimates provide further evidence of differences in the ESG–FDI slope across income groups, although both the magnitude and direction of this difference are sensitive to the inclusion of the Netherlands. Once the Netherlands is excluded, the estimated difference in slopes reverses, and the implied ESG coefficient for the high‐income group is no longer statistically significant. A similar sensitivity is observed in the linear and nonlinear specifications, indicating that the Netherlands plays an unusually influential role in the high‐income results, plausibly reflecting its position in international investment and financial‐routing networks. Taken as a whole, the findings suggest that the ESG–FDI relationship is better understood as context‐dependent rather than universal. They also underscore the importance of distinguishing robustness across model specifications from robustness to sample composition, particularly when aggregate FDI data include economies with substantial conduit investment activity.

title: Non-Commutative Rough Resource Dynamics (NC-RRD) Subsuming Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) and Critical Mineral Supply Chain Limits via UROA, STCT, and RQIG
summary: Critical mineral supply chains and Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) are conventionally bounded by linear resource depletion and static geopolitical risk models. This paper supersedes these views by establishing Non-Commutative Rough Resource Dynamics (NC-RRD) within the SMA-∞ Topos. By integrating Universal Rough Operator Algebra (UROA), the Seonggil Theory of Composite Torsion (STCT), and Rough Quantum Information Geometry (RQIG), we prove that lead-time delays and geographic processing concentration are macroscopic topological manifestations of non-commutative temporal-spatial shear stress.Furthermore, DLE processing and closed-loop recycling are formally derived as geodesic optimization sub-loops that stabilize the global resource manifold.

title: Knowledge‐Driven Supply Chain Digitalization and Fully Automated Baggage Handling System Success: The Mediating Role of Knowledge Integration Capability and the Moderating Role of Organizational Digital Readiness
summary: ABSTRACT The growing use of intelligent digital technologies is reshaping airport supply chains, but technology adoption alone does not explain why automated baggage handling initiatives succeed. knowledge‐driven supply chain digitalization (KSCD) is defined here as the organizational capability to use connected digital technologies and real‐time data to share information, coordinate decisions, and integrate baggage‐handling activities across airport supply‐chain actors. Fully Automated Baggage Handling System Success (FABHSS) is conceptualized as a multidimensional operational outcome reflected in efficiency, timely and reliable processing, routing accuracy and traceability, cross‐functional coordination, and overall support for baggage operations. Drawing on the Knowledge‐Based View and Dynamic Capability Theory (DCT), the study tested a moderated mediation model using survey data from 220 employees in airport operations, logistics, information technology, engineering, and baggage handling at major international airports in the United Arab Emirates. Covariance‐based structural equation modelling showed that KSCD positively influenced Knowledge Integration Capability (KIC; beta = 0.724, p < 0.001) and FABHSS (beta = 0.321, p < 0.001), while KIC positively influenced FABHSS (beta = 0.486, p < 0.001). Bootstrapping confirmed that KIC partially mediates the relationship between KSCD and FABHSS (indirect beta = 0.352, p < 0.001), and Organizational Digital Readiness strengthened the positive KSCD–KIC relationship (interaction beta = 0.184, p < 0.001). The findings show that automated baggage‐handling success depends on converting digitally generated information into integrated operational knowledge within a digitally ready organization.

summary: The paper assesses how the adoption of ESG principles in commercial banks affects credit policy and investment attractiveness. Using data of the Central Bank, the IMF and SQB, it examines ESG integration in the credit process, tensions with preferential lending (27% of the loan book) and microloans (23.9% of household lending), changes in funding (the share of issued securities rose from 2.4% to 4.4%) and bank privatization. ESG principles widen credit-risk management tools and access to foreign investors, but the lack of bank-level data prevents precise measurement of the effect.

title: The Impact of Green Technology Innovation on High‐Quality Economic Development and Its Mechanisms: Evidence From China
summary: ABSTRACT The imbalance between economic development and environmental protection has become a major challenge for regions seeking to achieve high quality economic development under China's new development philosophy. Can green technological innovation promote high quality economic development, and through what channels? How does fiscal decentralization shape this effect? To address these questions, this study uses panel data from 29 Chinese provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities and employs two‐way fixed‐effects and mediation‐effect models to systematically examine the overall effect of green technological innovation on high quality economic development, the moderating role of fiscal decentralization, and the underlying transmission mechanisms. The results show that green technological innovation significantly promotes high quality regional economic development, whereas fiscal decentralization significantly weakens this positive effect. The main effect of green technological innovation remains robust across multiple robustness tests. The mechanism analysis indicates that green technological innovation enhances high quality economic development by promoting energy conservation and emissions reduction and industrial structure upgrading. Grouped estimates further show that this positive effect is more pronounced in regions with more developed green finance, greater physical capital investment, and higher population density. This study provides useful empirical support and policy implications for improving the green innovation support system, optimizing local government incentive and constraint mechanisms, and advancing high quality economic development.

title: Profit Distribution Mechanisms for Investment Accounts in Malaysian Islamic Banks: An Analytical Study in Light of Shariah and Accounting Standards
summary: This study examines the profit distribution mechanisms for investment accounts in Malaysian Islamic banks. It analyzes the Shariah and accounting foundations that govern the relationship between the bank and investment account holders. The study identifies a set of fairness parameters rooted in Islamic legal principles and Islamic accounting standards, most notably: the requirement to predefine profit-sharing ratios, adherence to the Shariah rules of loss-bearing in mudarabah, full transparency and disclosure, proportional profit allocation based on investment amount and duration, and the governance rules relating to the use of the Profit Equalization Reserve (PER) and Investment Risk Reserve (IRR) to ensure that profit distribution does not compromise the integrity of profit-and-loss sharing. The study adopts a descriptive-analytical methodology, reviewing AAOIFI standards, Bank Negara Malaysia’s regulatory requirements, and practical banking applications related to investment fund management. The findings show that the Malaysian experience provides a structured and equitable model that reduces return volatility and strengthens compliance with the Islamic legal maxims “al-ghunm bil-ghurm” (gain is justified by risk) and “al-kharāj bi-al-ḍamān” (entitlement to return is contingent upon liability), while offering policy recommendations to enhance investor protection and ensure Shariahaligned fairness in profit distribution. The study further examines the Malaysian experience as an advanced model for segregating deposits from investment accounts, implementing the Rate of Return Framework, and managing investment accounts through the Investment Account Platform (IAP). This analysis highlights how far Malaysian Islamic banks have progressed in institutionalizing fairness parameters, compared with jurisdictions that lack a similarly robust governance framework.

title: Preference ≠ Tattooability: Auditing Reward Models for AI Tattoo Generation
summary: AI tattoo generation is usually ranked with the same reward models that rank general text-to-image outputs. Those models predict which image a crowd annotator prefers. A tattoo that will be worn also has to survive a needle, a gap that heals shut, and ink that spreads. We audited that gap with deterministic, physically scaled probes and with CLIPScore, PickScore, HPSv2.1 and ImageReward, on tattoo-subject pairs from HPDv2 and ImageRewardDB, on controlled defects, and on a print-scale ink-spread stress test. On HPDv2 tattoo-subject pairs, a-priori probes agree with human preference below chance, and that contrast remains after a Holm correction across scorers. Nothing here ranks a commercial AI tattoo generator. Competing interest: the author operates tatany.app; that product was not evaluated or ranked.

title: THE INFLUENCE OF CUSTOMER ORIENTATION, COMPETITOR ORIENTATION, AND GREEN ORGANIZATIONAL CULTURE ON MARKETING PERFORMANCE: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF GREEN INNOVATION WITH THE MODERATING EFFECT OF LEARNING ORGANIZATION IN PROPERTY DEVELOPMENT COMPANIES IN CENTRAL JAVA
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of customer orientation, competitor orientation, and green organizational culture on green innovation and marketing performance in property companies in Central Java. In addition, this study also examines the role of learning organization as a moderation variable that strengthens the relationship between these variables. A quantitative approach was used by a survey method of managers and marketing staff of property companies, and data analysis was carried out using the Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) technique.The results of the study show that customer orientation, competitor orientation, and green organizational culture have a positive and significant effect on green innovation and marketing performance. Green innovation has been proven to have a significant positive effect on marketing performance and mediate the influence of learning organization on marketing performance. In addition, learning organization also has a positive effect on marketing performance, as well as strengthening the influence of green innovation on increasing the company's competitiveness. title: Artificial Intelligence in the Social Media Strategies of UK Accounting Firms: An Evidence Synthesis and Protocol for a 21-Firm Mixed-Methods Study
summary: Accounting firms in the United Kingdom are adopting artificial intelligence (AI) across audit, tax, reporting and advisory work, yet little is known about how they use AI in social media, particularly on LinkedIn, to generate content, analyse engagement, schedule posts, personalise messages and generate leads. This article makes two contributions. First, it reports a structured synthesis of the most recent evidence from the Chartered Accountants Worldwide and ICAEW-linked survey, the Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), the Office for National Statistics, US industry research and the peer-reviewed literature, graded for evidential quality. Second, it presents a protocol for a convergent mixed-methods study of 21 UK accounting firms. The synthesis shows rapid but uneven adoption: about 35% of UK businesses with ten or more employees used AI in June 2026; 85% of surveyed chartered accountants were at least fairly willing to use it; larger organisations used AI for analysis and reporting more than sole practitioners and small and medium practices; yet 66% of respondents had received no employer AI training, and fewer than a third of AI-using organisations had policies on transparency, explainability or bias. No study located measures AI use in the social media strategy of accounting firms. The protocol specifies the sampling, instruments, analysis and ethics needed to close that gap. Implications for firms are offered as testable hypotheses: begin with narrow, governed applications, keep a named professional accountable for published content, and measure net rather than gross benefit.

title: VTAS-Hybrid v2.1: Statistically Audited Predictive Thresholding for Optical Tape Storage
summary: VTAS-Hybrid (v2.0.0) – TECHNICAL RESEARCH REPORT AND SYSTEM SPECIFICATION 1. ABSTRACT Modern data centers face severe scaling and sustainability challenges regarding cold data archiving. Conventional magnetic tapes (LTO) and optical media suffer from signal degradation and physical wear over decades. This paper introduces VTAS-Hybrid (v2.0.0), a major second-generation software-hardware co-design architecture that shifts the burden of archival longevity from pure material perfection to adaptive statistical signal processing. Instead of assuming static material properties or relying on blind mathematical models, the VTAS-Hybrid architecture introduces a software-driven execution loop directly into the readout drive. The system decouples signal processing into two distinct quality gates: an absolute readability evaluation based on standardized distance metrics (d'), and a differential degradation test driven by a Welch–Satterthwaite t-test. By dynamically estimating the noise floor from embedded pilot symbols, the engine monitors physical media wear in real time and generates a bit-level erasure uncertainty map. This outputs a precise reliability framework directly to subsequent Error Correction Coding (ECC) layers, maximizing data recovery performance without hardware modification. 2. THE TECHNICAL PROBLEM TO BE SOLVED As physical storage media ages under long-term data center conditions, the optical signal levels representing digital zeros and ones drift toward each other. Localized material anomalies, such as surface scratches, dust, or polymer relaxation, induce optical scattering. This phenomenon simultaneously attenuates high-level signals (digital ones) and raises the noise floor of low-level signals (digital zeros) due to scattering reflections. Consequently, the signal distributions physically overlap, blinding conventional fixed-threshold readout drives. Current storage architectures fail under these conditions in three distinct ways: Static Thresholds expect factory-fresh material characteristics and fail to adapt to long-term signal decay. Blind Predictive Models (relying purely on historical mathematical aging curves) fail whenever the real-world material batch varies from ideal laboratory conditions. Simple Moving Averages drift blindly based on the local data pattern payload itself (e.g., during long consecutive strings of digital zeros) and exhibit a destructive phase lag when encountering sharp, localized scratches. 3. TECHNICAL OPERATION OF THE SYSTEM (FOUR STAGES) The VTAS-Hybrid (v2.0.0) architecture eliminates these operational biases by replacing speculative models with continuous, real-time, and heavily guarded statistical measurements. The hardware execution sequence flows through four robust stages: Stage 1: Initial Calibration (Static Baseline) Prior to executing data read operations, the drive scans a designated, noisy reference area at the beginning of the media containing a known pilot bit sequence. The engine estimates the empirical mean and noise variance for each bit class independently. The system includes an explicit hardware safeguard that immediately aborts and invalidates the calibration if the measurement variance is zero or if the logical ordering is inverted (i.e., if the digital one level falls below the digital zero level). Stage 2: Absolute Readability Test (d'-prime Quality Gate) Known pilot symbols are embedded at regular intervals between data blocks. The readout drive utilizes these pilots to calculate a standardized distance metric (the d'-prime/Cohen’s d value). If a severe scratch has forced the signal levels to merge so deeply into the noise floor that reliable separation is mathematically impossible, the system bypasses guessing and immediately flags a secure HARD_FAILURE state. Stage 3: Differential Degradation Test (Welch–Satterthwaite t-test) If the local section passes the absolute d'-prime quality gate, the algorithm compares the local signal separation against the initial global calibration. This differential comparison utilizes a combined standard error ($SE_{\Delta}$) that accounts for the statistical uncertainty of both the baseline calibration and the real-time pilot measurement. Because the pilot sample size is small, effective degrees of freedom are dynamically calculated via the Welch–Satterthwaite approximation, and the critical threshold is derived from a Student’s t-distribution. If the signal separation has shrunk with statistical significance, a degradation state (SUSPECT_DAMAGE) is triggered, and a new, optimized local threshold is deployed. Stage 4: Dynamic Symbol-Level Erasure Masking During data bit quantization, the drive measures the exact distance of each analog signal sample from the selected decision boundary. If a sample falls too close to the boundary due to noise, it is flagged as highly uncertain via an erasure bit-mask. This masking engine operates independently of the block status: under NORMAL operations, it masks only the most extreme marginal anomalies, but under SUSPECT_DAMAGE states, the threshold distance is automatically tightened. This outputs a precise real-time truth map of data reliability directly to the subsequent Error Correction Coding (ECC) engine, maximizing its erasure decoding performance. 4. SYSTEM SAFEGUARDS (EMBEDDED SOFTWARE ROBUSTNESS) The architecture integrates strict industrial-grade software protections to prevent runtime exceptions and silent data corruption: Type Constraints: The algorithm strictly validates and isolates raw data arrays. It blocks implicit language type-coercions (such as boolean values implicitly converting to integers), preventing statistical distortion of the sample size. Finiteness Auditing: The engine explicitly traps measurements and aborts execution if inputs contain numerical anomalies such as Not-a-Number (NaN) or infinity (Inf). Reality Validation: Decision boundaries and noise estimations must be strictly real scalars. The engine immediately rejects complex numbers, which would otherwise crash logical comparison operators in physical drive hardware. Length Verification: The decoder enforces that the incoming data sector length matches the hardware block size constraint exactly. Truncated or malformed sectors force an immediate fallback to prevent decoding alignment failures. 5. The Welch–Satterthwaite approximation assumes that the global calibration samples and local real-time pilots are statistically independent and uncorrelated. 2. If temporal correlation exists, the nominal significance level (alpha) may deviate. 3. The min_d_prime threshold and erasure scaling coefficients are experimental design parameters subject to optimization via systematic benchmarking. must be a positive integer scalar.") if not (0.0 < significance_level < 0.5): raise ValueError("Significance level (alpha) must be bounded between (0.0, 0.5).") if not isinstance(min_d_prime, (int, self.se_global_sq = None self.global_th = None def _validate_bits(self, bits_input): """Strict bit vector validation: enforces binary 0 or 1, rejects booleans and strings.""" try: arr = summary: This study aims to explore the role of social cohesion, media, higher education, empowerment, and interfaith harmony in good governance of the public universities in Pakistan. title: The Influence of ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) on The Firm Value of The Banking Sector in ASEAN-5 Countries 2021–2024
summary: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations have become increasingly important in investment decisions; however, their relationship with firm value in the banking sector remains inconsistent across markets. This study examined the relationship between ESG performance and firm value among listed banks in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and the Philippines during the 2021–2024 period. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data obtained from annual reports, sustainability reports, and the Refinitiv database. Purposive sampling resulted in a sample of 28 banks, yielding 112 firm-year observations. Firm value was measured using Tobin’s Q, while sustainability performance was represented by the aggregate ESG score and the individual environmental, social, and governance pillar scores. Panel-data regression analysis was conducted using EViews 12, with model specification tests supporting fixed-effects estimation and robust standard errors applied to the aggregate ESG model. The results revealed a positive and statistically significant association between aggregate ESG performance and firm value, with a coefficient of 0.0026. However, none of the individual environmental, social, or governance pillars exhibited a statistically significant association with firm value in the pillar-level model. These findings suggest that integrated ESG performance may provide valuation-relevant information, although the results do not establish investor perceptions or causal mechanisms. The study concludes that stronger aggregate ESG performance is associated with higher firm value among the sampled ASEAN-5 banks and provides empirical evidence that may inform corporate sustainability strategies and investment assessments in the banking sector.

title: A Unified OPEN/CLOSED/EXTERNAL Audit Framework Across Seven Mathematical Conjectures
summary: This publication presents a comparative formal auditing framework applied to seven major mathematical research problems: the Riemann Hypothesis, P versus NP, Navier–Stokes regularity, Yang–Mills existence and mass gap, the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture, the Hodge Conjecture, and the Beal Conjecture.The framework examines the relationships between OPEN_MATH, CLOSED_MATH, formal bridge conditions, terminal proof obligations, and EXTERNAL certification states through a unified analytical procedure.Each research domain is evaluated using common criteria for mathematical closure, dependency completeness, certificate provenance, reproducibility, and the identification of unresolved terminal conditions.The study distinguishes structurally verified proof components from conditional reductions and unconditional mathematical demonstrations. Historical source commits, audit records, and certificate references support the comparison.The purpose of this work is to provide a systematic method for comparing formal proof progress and certification boundaries across distinct mathematical problems.The presence of an EXTERNAL state within a formal system does not, by itself, establish an unconditional solution to the corresponding mathematical conjecture.
